content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Yoseph Linde renewed his support of Dana-Farber with a recent gift of $100,000 to advance bile duct cancer research under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. This latest gift, in honor of his late wife Haya, supports Cleary’s team’s continued in-depth DNA and RNA sequencing work to better understand which therapies work best against each subtype of bile duct cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people outside on a balcony

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein made a generous gift in support of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole M. and Philip L. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. The gift will support Jänne and his team’s continued research into targeted therapies in lung cancer, novel EGFR inhibitors, and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: $10 million gift brings rare cancers to the fore
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Linde Family Foundation has made a transformative $10 million gift to Dana-Farber to launch the Center for Therapeutic Discovery, which will develop novel therapies for patients with rare and hard-to-treat cancers.

img.alt_text: Graphic depiction of MLL complex proteins

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Russ and his late wife, Paula, established the Project P Fund in 2014 with a goal of empowering researchers at Dana-Farber to develop more effective targeted and immune-based therapies for patients with colorectal cancer. Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Jonathan Mehlman gave $100,000, honoring his late wife Marla, in support of breast cancer research under the direction of Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH. With this funding, Tolaney and her team will continue developing new clinical approaches for the most aggressive forms of breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Judy and Peter Kovler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through the Judy & Peter Blum Kovler Foundation, Judy and Peter Kovler recently made a gift of $100,000, bringing their total giving to critical initiatives to $450,000. Their new gift supports research led by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, to accelerate new treatments for invasive lobular carcinoma, a difficult-to-diagnose breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

Summer 2024
By Kayla Carcone

The Melanoma Research Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber’s Pere Puigserver, PhD, with a prestigious $200,000 Established Investigator Award. Puigserver’s pioneering research aims to revolutionize immunotherapeutic approaches for metastatic melanoma, with a focus on overcoming drug resistance and improving patient survival outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Eileen Greisch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Malcolm and Luli MacNaught
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent gift of $100,000, Malcolm and Luli MacNaught continued their steadfast support for Dana-Farber’s F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, a pioneer in groundbreaking treatments for melanoma. Among these is the recent trial of a new combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors that allowed patients with metastatic melanoma to survive…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Bill and Mary Michels gave $170,000 in support of the Suzanne Michels Obenshain Fund for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Research at Dana-Farber. The couple made this generous donation in honor of their daughter Suzanne, who passed away from the disease in 2020.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: The National Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Breast Cancer Foundation has made a generous gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as part of their ongoing support. This latest gift plays a crucial role in advancing our mission to defy cancer and enhance breast cancer patient outcomes.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Changing the trajectory of multiple myeloma and access to care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Joan Suzanne Tomsich was just 48 years old, she thought her life was over. A diagnosis of multiple myeloma led her to thoughts like, “Will I be around to see my kids graduate or witness them getting married?”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Anna Fuller Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Anna Fuller Fund has made a wonderful impact with a $150,000 gift to support breast cancer research conducted by Evanna Mills, PhD, at Dana-Farber. The investment will fuel investigations to better understand risk factors for triple-negative breast cancer with the potential to inform the development of more effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Falmouth Road Race team surpasses $10 million milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On August 20, more than 325 participants laced up on behalf of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to compete in the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

img.alt_text: A Falmouth Road Race runner poses for a photo

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Kayla Carcone

The Muscular Dystrophy Association has awarded a $300,000 grant to support research led by Pere Puigserver, PhD, at Dana-Farber, addressing the absence of effective treatments for mitochondrial myopathies. The study will investigate the efficacy of tetracyclines, a class of antibiotics, as another method to treat these diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Gastroenterological Association
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Gastroenterological Association awarded $300,000 to support a Dana-Farber study into pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), an aggressive disease that currently has limited and short-lasting treatment options. This funding will enable Jeffrey Patterson-Fortin, MD, PhD, to gain insights into how PDAC responds to immune-based therapies that could provide longer term…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR targets breast and uterine cancers

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Kayla McMahon

Hockey goalies across the nation raised $100,000 for Dana-Farber through October Saves by gathering pledges for each save during Breast Cancer Awareness Month. These funds support the pediatric leukemia research of Scott Armstrong, MD, PhD (pictured far left), and Wallace Bourgeois, MD (second from left), in honor of Charlie Capalbo, a Connecticut goalie and Dana-Farber patient who passed away from leukemia at age 23 in 2022. Presenting the check were Lara Hopewell, CEO and Founder of October Saves, and two New England goalies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon supports bold research by emerging talent
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded $1.22 million in grants to four early career investigators at Dana-Farber whose research has the potential to yield important breakthroughs in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dolecki Family gives back to advance pediatric cancer therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Charlotte Dolecki passed away, she had a provision in her trust for charity. The trustee—her great-nephew, Vincent Dello-Iacono—and her great-niece, Danielle Comella, immediately knew where they wanted to make a gift.

img.alt_text: The Dolecki Family presents a ceremonial check to Lisa Scherber, director of patient and family programs in the Jimmy Fund Clinic, and Scott Armstrong, MD, PhD.

Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

PHASE ONE Foundation awarded $370,000 to support a Dana-Farber clinical trial led by Alison O’Neill, MD. The clinical trial aims to test a new intratumoral delivery method for a novel immunotherapy in pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Rathburn
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a generous $150,000 gift, David Rathburn (pictured), through the Rathburn Family Foundation, supported a clinical trial led by Dana-Farber’s Benjamin Schlechter, MD. The clinical trial aims to expand the benefits of immunotherapy to more colorectal cancer patients, with a specific focus on reducing unwanted side effects of these therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation helps advance glioblastoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation has awarded $524,081 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to advance novel immunotherapy approaches to treat glioblastoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Ambrose Monell Foundation fuels critical immunotherapy priorities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: By encouraging strategic risk-taking and rewarding experimentation and new ideas, the Ambrose Monell Foundation is empowering Dana-Farber to capitalize on its collective expertise to develop a new generation of innovative cancer-fighting immunotherapies tailored to the specific needs of patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grant fuels pediatric brain tumor research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A recent $600,000 ChadTough Defeat DIPG Game Changer Grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute aims to expand treatment options for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG).

Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Frank Walsh

With a generous $150,000 gift, David Rathburn (pictured), through the Rathburn Family Foundation, supported a clinical trial led by Dana-Farber’s Benjamin Schlechter, MD. The clinical trial aims to expand the benefits of immunotherapy to more colorectal cancer patients, with a specific focus on reducing unwanted side effects of these therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PHASE ONE Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PHASE ONE Foundation awarded $370,000 to support a Dana-Farber clinical trial led by Alison O’Neill, MD. The clinical trial aims to test a new intratumoral delivery method for a novel immunotherapy in pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Russ Agrusa honors late wife by fueling colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Russ and his late wife, Paula, established the Project P Fund in 2014 with a goal of empowering researchers at Dana-Farber to develop more effective targeted and immune-based therapies for patients with colorectal cancer. Since Paula’s death in 2016, Russ has continued to honor her legacy through ongoing support for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Ambrose Monell Foundation fuels critical immunotherapy priorities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: By encouraging strategic risk-taking and rewarding experimentation and new ideas, the Ambrose Monell Foundation is empowering Dana-Farber to capitalize on its collective expertise to develop a new generation of innovative cancer-fighting immunotherapies tailored to the specific needs of patients.

Summer 2024
By Robbie Merritt

The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes of melanoma. Pictured, Lena Maximo Robinson and Richard Robinson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brian and Jane Crowley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Martin family’s events surpass $1 million milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber celebrated the more than $1 million cumulatively raised by the family of the late Sharon Crowley Martin through events including Derby Day, a Kentucky Derby-themed cocktail watch party.

img.alt_text: The Martin family receiving an award

jetpack-related-posts.title: Derby Day
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Siblings Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin once again hosted their Derby Day fundraiser in memory of their mother, Sharon Crowley Martin, who passed away from melanoma in 2007. They raised $143,000 to advance the vital research of Dana-Farber’s Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma, F. Stephen Hodi Jr.,…

img.alt_text: A crowd of people inside a tent with colorful globe lights

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Malcolm and Luli MacNaught
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent gift of $100,000, Malcolm and Luli MacNaught continued their steadfast support for Dana-Farber’s F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, a pioneer in groundbreaking treatments for melanoma. Among these is the recent trial of a new combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors that allowed patients with metastatic melanoma to survive…

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Robert Bray Portrait Design

Lori and David Scragg made a gift of $300,000 to support the Lynch Syndrome Center at Dana-Farber, a comprehensive multidisciplinary cancer genetics group that specializes in coordinating the care of people with Lynch syndrome, a genetic condition linked to cancer that affects about 1 in 300 people in the U.S.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

St. Baldrick’s Foundation renewed their support for Dana-Farber with grants totaling nearly $200,000 to fund studies that will lay the groundwork for better precision medicine approaches for children with leukemia. These projects, led by Dana-Farber, involve collaboration with multiple institutions in the U.S. and abroad.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As part of their mission to fund innovative research at top institutions around the country, the Lymphoma Research Foundation’s recent funding cycle included awarding grants totaling $115,000 to fund two Dana-Farber studies into advanced treatment options for patients diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma and mantle cell lymphoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CLL Global Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. This funding will help advance their studies of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aiming to uncover new insights and improve treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation recently made grants totaling $200,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to fund two studies. One explores circulating tumor DNA at critical timepoints in early stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and the second assesses how chemotherapy effects the tumor-immune microenvironment and estrogen receptor activity in young…

Summer 2024
By Kayla McMahon

Swim Across America hosted its 28th annual Boston Open Water Swim event, which directly benefits Dana-Farber patients and families. Swimmers of all ages and skills levels united to “Make Waves Against Cancer” and raised $175,000, bringing the event’s cumulative fundraising total to over $3 million to date.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America raised $250,000 in 2024 to benefit Dana-Farber’s Perini Family Survivors’ Center. Since 1996, the Boston Open Water Swim has united swimmers of all ages and abilities, raising over $3.5 million in total to support vital survivorship research at Dana-Farber and continuing to “Make Waves Against Cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 27 years, Swim Across America has supported Dana-Farber through events like their annual Boston Open Water Swim event. In 2022, swimmers of all ages and skill levels raised $142,000 to help support cancer research and care at the Institute, for a lifetime total of more than $3 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America’s Boston Open Water Swim raised $335,000 in 2025 to benefit patients who receive care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and their families. Raising over $3.8 million since 1996, the organization continues to “Make Waves to Fight Cancer” and fuel critical survivorship research at Dana-Farber. This year's event will…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk steps into record-breaking year with over $11.2 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On a sunny Sunday in October 2025, the Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s signature fundraising event, crossed more than just the finish line at Boston Common.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s Boston half team sets new record
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sunday, November 9, marked the Boston Athletic Association’s (B.A.A.’s) annual Boston Half, a scenic 13.1-mile race through Franklin Park and the Emerald Necklace Park System.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® celebrates 40 years of support for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ice cream lovers of all ages were invited to Patriot Place in Foxborough, Mass., to celebrate the 40th annual Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM.

The Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation gave $200,000 in support of the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP) at Dana-Farber. With these funds, the CCEP team will continue to address disparities in health care for underserved populations and pursue equitable care for every cancer patient.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding equitable access to critical care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last year, the National Breast Cancer Foundation (NBCF) generously provided $155,000 to support Dana-Farber’s inclusion, diversity, and equity work to ensure equitable health outcomes for all.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Burlingame Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Burlingame Foundation gave $300,000 to provide support for patient navigation through the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP). Patient navigation involves supporting and assisting patients through the complexities of treatment—a key component of the CCEP’s effort to address disparities in cancer care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Yawkey Foundation’s heartfelt support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Yawkey Foundation is a longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, stemming from the historic relationship between the Jimmy Fund and the Boston Red Sox. Perpetuating the philanthropic legacy of the team’s owners, Tom and Jean Yawkey, the foundation made gifts totaling $180,000 in 2024.

img.alt_text: Two people holding ice cream outside a Cookie Monstah food truck

Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

With a total contribution of more than $230,000, Wipe Out Kids’ Cancer is supporting two Dana-Farber researchers as they work to enhance treatment options for children with leukemia. One study aims to improve the recovery process for stem cell transplant patients, while the other is testing a new combination therapy in T-ALL that also could have therapeutic benefits for many forms of pediatric cancer.

title.rendered: Boston Marathon<sup>®</sup> Jimmy Fund Walk celebrates 35 years of inspiration and impact

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Casey Reis
Photography by Josh Campbell and Bryce Vickmark

Last fall, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patients, families, and supporters joined forces to defy cancer at the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, which raises the most money of any single-day walk in the nation. Year after year, dedicated walkers gather on the world-famous Boston Marathon® course for a day of hope, unity, and inspiration, fueling critical advancements in cancer treatment. The October 1 event was marked by more than 8,400 enthusiastic participants coming together to raise a record-breaking $9.4 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign and provide critical momentum to innovative scientific discovery and compassionate patient care. It was a milestone year for Dana-Farber’s signature event, propelling the Walk’s cumulative fundraising total to more than $176 million raised since its inception in 1989.

The Walk served as a magnificent capstone to the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary year, and a reminder of the power of its grassroots community. Walkers, corporate sponsors, volunteers, and their supporters all played a pivotal role in the event’s success, including presenting sponsor Hyundai, which has supported the Walk since 1998.

Jimmy Fund Walk participants could walk virtually in a location of their choice or from a distance along the Boston Marathon course—ranging from a 5K to a 26.2-mile marathon—with all in-person routes culminating in a finish line celebration. Along the course, walkers were supported by more than 700 volunteers and treated to complimentary snacks and water provided by generous sponsors. Traditionally, finish line festivities take place at Copley Square in Boston, but with construction underway at the landmark site, it shifted to the Fenway Park neighborhood. There, walkers celebrated 35 years of progress with lively music, food, motivational speeches, and more within view of the historic baseball stadium.

Kristy Spears led team #MaleiaStrong in a virtual Jimmy Fund Walk in her hometown of Crestview, Fla. Kristy walks in memory of her daughter Maleia, a pediatric brain tumor patient who was treated in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic. “It is the best place to be when faced with the horrific, life-changing words, ‘Your child has cancer,’” Kristy says.

“It was an opportunity to give back to a place that had given us extra time and memories with our beloved daughter.”

Kristy Spears

The closeness and camaraderie of the Jimmy Fund Walk drew Kristy in. “The walkers are there due to a direct connection to someone who has been well-loved and cared for at Dana-Farber. After our daughter surrendered her fight, getting involved simply felt natural. It was an opportunity to give back to a place that had given us extra time and memories with our beloved daughter.” Since the team’s inaugural Walk in 2022, #MaleiaStrong has raised more than $70,600.

Each dollar raised by walkers like Kristy adds up to an extraordinary sum that will significantly impact the future of cancer care. While a lot has changed in the 35 years since the first Jimmy Fund Walk, its growing community remains profoundly bonded by a fierce determination to defy cancer—in honor of the patients they walk for, and in the spirit of those who walked before them.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

title.rendered: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Amber Sinicrope
Photography by Justin Knight

In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades. Dana-Farber’s highest honor, the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award was established in 1968 in appreciation of the contributions Sidney Farber, MD, made to medicine and to the development and support of cancer care and research around the world.

The Hale Family name has become synonymous with Dana-Farber’s focused efforts to understand, prevent, and treat pancreatic cancer, and their philanthropy has made the Institute a worldwide leader and pioneer in this work. “It is a disease that really needs champions,” says Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, director of the Hale Family Center for Pancreatic Cancer Research and of the Gastrointestinal Cancer Center, and the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. “The Hale Family’s commitment to making an impact has built a foundation of collaboration and innovation that has accelerated pancreatic cancer research, translated discoveries to the clinic, and improved patient outcomes.”

“When pancreatic cancer is no more, I hope that the Hale Center will have been a leader in this victory.”

Judy Hale

The Hale Family’s support of Dana-Farber honors the memory of Judy’s late husband, Robert “Bob” T. Hale Sr., who was a generous philanthropist in his own right and who was treated at Dana-Farber for pancreatic cancer.

In 2007, Bob and Judy Hale established the Robert T. Hale Sr. and Judith B. Hale Fund for Pancreatic Research. In 2012, Judy made a $10 million gift to establish the Hale Family Center for Pancreatic Cancer and name the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. The Hale Family’s commitment to research and care has continued across the generations as Judy, along with her son and daughter-in-law, Rob and Karen, made an additional $15 million gift in 2016, and a tremendous $50 million gift in 2021 to establish and further support the Hale Family Center for Pancreatic Cancer Research. This latest gift represents the largest single gift to pancreatic cancer research in the Institute’s history and one of the largest gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign. With this gift, the Hale Family’s cumulative giving to Dana-Farber surpassed $80 million, making them the second largest individual donors to the Institute.

So much of Dana-Farber’s progress in pancreatic cancer can be traced to the Hale Family’s involvement and leadership. “With the Hales’ support, we are pushing the frontiers of what is possible, and we will not rest until we find cures for this devastating disease—for all the patients we serve today, and those all around the world who look to us for hope,” reflects Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, president and CEO of Dana-Farber and the Richard and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine.

While this award is embedded in Judy’s heart forever, she continues to focus on the biggest prize of all: “I am thinking big and hope to make a difference in erasing this miserable disease for everyone around the globe. When pancreatic cancer is no more, I hope that the Hale Center will have been a leader in this victory.”

title.rendered: Jimmy Fund Golf community helps to usher in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Robbie Merritt
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign. Through more than 140 tournaments and events, participants proved that everyone can make a difference in Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund’s lifesaving mission to defy cancer.

It was a particularly exciting time to be involved with the program, as 2023 also marked the 75th anniversary of the Jimmy Fund itself. Since 1983, funds raised through Jimmy Fund Golf have turned groundbreaking research into lifesaving treatments for adults and children with all forms of cancer.

“Jimmy Fund Golf is essential to the impact our larger Jimmy Fund community has had on cancer research and care at Dana-Farber over the last 75 years,” says Suzanne Fountain, vice president of the Jimmy Fund. “The funds raised from the fairways have directly moved the needle closer to a world without cancer.”

Learn more about all 2023 tournaments.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Elina Tonkova
Photography by Sam Ogden and Bryce Vickmark

With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients. In the United States, longstanding structural inequities drive social determinants of health—the conditions and environments in which people are born, live, and work—resulting in striking disparities in cancer incidence and outcomes. As an international leader across the continuum of cancer research and care, Dana-Farber is dedicated to being on the forefront of initiatives aimed at reducing disparities and ensuring that expert, innovative, and compassionate care is accessible and effective for everyone.

In the adult cancer setting, Lathan and the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP) team aim to provide those who have been historically excluded from receiving equitable access to health care with streamlined pathways to Dana-Farber’s expert and integrated care. Key initiatives of the CCEP include the expansion of Dana-Farber’s community-focused patient navigators who identify and engage—as early as possible—those patients facing socioeconomic and structural barriers to care who would benefit from rapid, personalized support.

The Scarlet Feather Fund’s gift is also supporting the launch of a pilot “Ambulatory Safety Net” focused on mitigating risk of missed and delayed cancer screening and follow-up to abnormal test results. This new pilot program, planned in collaboration with community hospital partners of Dana-Farber – Merrimack Valley, one of Dana-Farber’s regional campuses serving the Institute’s largest population of historically marginalized patients, will help ensure the timely completion of cancer screening and connection to specialty care. Lastly, the gift will assist with the expansion of CCEP’s on-site cancer diagnostics clinics at Federally Qualified Health Centers.

Bona’s research has shown that children with cancer who live in poverty have higher rates of relapse and lower survival, even when treated on the same clinical trials. How pediatric oncologists can intervene to mitigate this risk of relapse is the focus of research being supported by the Scarlet Feather Fund. The gift supports Bona’s team in developing the first health equity interventions ever designed or tested in childhood cancer that target risk factors like food or transportation insecurity—a process similar to developing new drugs to target tumor characteristics. “This funding is speeding the development of a portfolio of these novel interventions,” says Bona, “and has concurrently allowed us to strategize how we will sustain effective pediatric health equity interventions once we develop them.” 

Philanthropy is critical to the success of these care and research initiatives. By supporting these projects, the Scarlet Feather Fund and other philanthropic partners are strengthening Dana-Farber’s ability to ensure that adult and pediatric patients from historically marginalized communities have equitable paths to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Advancing equity tops agenda at Women’s Leadership Breakfast
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 220 business and community leaders attended the Women’s Leadership Breakfast hosted by the Executive Council of the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber faculty and staff speakers at the Women’s Leadership Breakfast hosted by the Executive Council of the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers

jetpack-related-posts.title: Krafts champion early detection and prevention for at-risk communities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a gift of $5 million to The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Kraft Family will bring Dana-Farber’s lifesaving early detection and prevention programs to more people at risk of developing cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society enables pathbreaking new inquiries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Recent grants from the American Cancer Society fund innovative projects across Dana-Farber, from basic science to pediatric cancer disparities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. title.rendered: The Mark Foundation spurs innovation in immunotherapy

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kathy Clute

The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded Dana-Farber investigator Catherine Wu, MD, and two investigators at the Broad Institute a $3 million, three-year grant to further their research into personalized, T cell-directed cancer immunotherapy.

Wu and her Broad Institute colleagues are one of four teams selected for The Mark Foundation’s 2023 Endeavor Awards. The goal of these prestigious grants, the foundation says, is “to support teams of scientists tackling a range of urgent challenges in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer.” Since 2021, the cancer-focused nonprofit has distributed $30 million in Endeavor Awards “to accelerate progress in high-priority research areas through a collaborative approach.”

“The Mark Foundation is committed to supporting the most exciting projects in cancer research.”

Ryan Schoenfeld, PhD, The Mark Foundation

Wu is the chief of Dana-Farber’s Division of Stem Cell Transplantation and Cellular Therapies and a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies. She and her team are working to better understand the biological mechanisms behind potentially lifesaving T cell-directed therapies that kill cancer cells and tumors. While such therapies have been transformative for some patients, several factors prevent them from being more widely effective, particularly against solid tumors.

The researchers are using samples from patients with colorectal cancer and high-grade serous ovarian cancer to develop new ways of boosting the efficacy of tumor-reactive T cells (TCRs). By better understanding how T cells function to eliminate tumors, the team hopes to translate their findings into personalized and shared therapies.

“Immunotherapy has been helpful against certain cancers like melanoma, but we have not had the same success across all cancer types, and it’s essential to understand why,” said Wu. “We’re looking at several central questions: What are the antigen targets for TCRs? How do T cell clones interact with the tumor microenvironment? And what is the optimal state of T cells for lasting tumor suppression?”

The team’s work will build on their previous innovations, which make it possible to rapidly identify a patient’s TCRs and then reprogram those cells so that they are toxic to cancer cells without damaging healthy ones.

“The Mark Foundation is committed to supporting the most exciting projects in cancer research throughout their life cycle,” said Mark Foundation CEO Ryan Schoenfeld, PhD. “I cannot wait to see what highly personalized, lifesaving treatments will come from the work Dr. Wu and her team are doing.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dale Fishman
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dale Fishman gave $243,000 to fuel pioneering research led by Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD; Catherine Wu, MD; and physician-scientists across Dana-Farber. Fishman’s multifaceted philanthropy is empowering these investigators to advance novel cellular therapies for pancreatic cancer and personalized cancer vaccines, while bolstering the Faculty Research Fund, which together pave the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Beerman Family Fund fuels next-generation approach to cancer vaccines
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gift may help speed production, reduce cost, and increase personalization of cancer vaccines to be more effective in many types of cancers.

img.alt_text: Two people outside in front of trees and bushes

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

title.rendered: Investment in infrastructure accelerates immunotherapy development

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Robin Orwant

The Massachusetts Life Sciences Center (MLSC) has granted Dana-Farber $2.78 million to build crucial infrastructure for developing immunotherapies—novel treatments that leverage the immune system to fight cancer.

Co-principal investigators Eric Smith, MD, PhD, director of Translational Research for Immune Effector Cell Therapies; William Hahn, MD, PhD, the William Rosenberg Professor of Medicine; and Xin Zhou, PhD, received the grant through the MLSC’s Research Infrastructure Program. The funds will be used to purchase state-of-the-art equipment that will significantly expand Dana-Farber’s capacity to bring more of these lifesaving therapies to patients as quickly as possible.

Over the past few decades, the FDA has approved more than 100 immunotherapies, which have improved survival for many patients and have even induced complete remissions in certain advanced, previously intractable forms of cancer. Recent technological advances promise to accelerate unprecedented progress in the development of these transformative therapies. However, because the use of these new technologies requires highly specialized knowledge across several different fields of expertise, scientists have found it difficult to establish the cross-disciplinary collaborations needed to capitalize on these technological breakthroughs.

“The MLSC grant will significantly expand IMPACT2’s capacity to support multiple projects in parallel from various Massachusetts academic and industry groups.”

Eric Smith, MD, PhD

This challenge is being addressed through a new Immunotherapy Platform for Antibody and CAR Therapeutics Discovery and Translation (IMPACT2) research program, led by Smith and his colleagues, including IMPACT2 head of research Anusuya Ramasubramanian, PhD. Housed in a newly constructed space at the Institute, IMPACT2 focuses on providing centralized, accessible, cross-disciplinary expertise and infrastructure required to engineer, test, and optimize new cancer-fighting immunotherapies.

“The MLSC grant will significantly expand IMPACT2’s capacity to support multiple projects in parallel from various Massachusetts academic and industry groups,” said Smith. “Ultimately, this will enhance our ability to rapidly and robustly develop new immunotherapies that could revolutionize treatment for patients with many different types of cancer.”

The MLSC is an economic development and investment agency whose multi-pronged mission is to serve as the hub of the Massachusetts life sciences ecosystem; encourage innovation through investments in good science and business; strengthen and protect Massachusetts’ global leadership position in the life sciences; accelerate the commercialization of promising treatments, therapies, and cures that will improve patient care; create jobs; and drive economic and workforce development in science and technology. Its Research Infrastructure Program provides grants for capital projects that enable and support life sciences research and development in the Commonwealth.  “The MLSC invests in the scientific infrastructure required to bring cutting edge diagnostics and therapies to patients,” said Carla Reimold, PhD, MLSC’s vice president of industry strategy and investments. “By leveraging the expertise of the Dana-Farber team, this grant will enable new discoveries and improve patients’ lives.”

title.rendered: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Jodi Hyer
Photography by Sam Ogden

The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies. Rather than targeting cancer-causing genetic mutations directly, epigenetic therapies target specialized proteins that can turn off cancer-causing genes inside cells.

Kimberly Stegmaier, MD, vice chair of Pediatric Oncology Research and the Ted Williams Chair at Dana-Farber, will leverage her V Foundation Pediatric Cancer All-Star Award for research that aims to unlock the potential of a novel epigenetic therapy for neuroblastoma. This work builds upon Stegmaier’s recent discovery that a common form of high-risk neuroblastoma depends on a group of epigenetic proteins known as the SAGA complex to alter the expression of genes that are critical for neuroblastoma cell survival. Although drugs targeting SAGA are in development, none have been tested in neuroblastoma. The grant will enable Stegmaier to initiate critical preclinical testing of SAGA-targeted drugs for this disease.

Stegmaier also plans to identify effective drug combinations that can be used with SAGA-targeted inhibitors. The goal of this critical preclinical research is to validate the SAGA complex as an effective target, thereby accelerating SAGA inhibitors into clinical trials as a novel therapeutic approach for children with high-risk neuroblastoma.

Sarah Johnstone, MD, PhD, will use her 2023 Women Scientists Innovation Award for Cancer Research, a V Scholar grant, to study two “architectural” proteins, BORIS and CTCF, which normally bind to and induce structural changes in DNA in order to regulate gene expression. BORIS and CTCF are commonly mutated in ovarian cancer, but how these mutations might affect DNA structure and gene expression to promote this cancer is unknown. Johnstone’s novel research will generate cellular models to study how BORIS and CTCF mutations impact DNA structure and subsequent gene expression, and then pinpoint the key therapeutic pathways involved. The goal is to identify urgently needed new therapeutic approaches for ovarian cancer, a cancer with high recurrence rates and standard-of-care treatment regimens that have remained unchanged for over two decades.

V Foundation Vice President of Grants and Research Kara Coleman, PhD, says, “We are proud to fund projects that will change the future of cancer research and improve patient lives. We are confident that Dr. Stegmaier and Dr. Johnstone’s work will help us achieve that goal. Both researchers have brought novel ideas to their respective fields, and we are thrilled that V Foundation grants will be instrumental in driving forward this lifesaving research.”

title.rendered: The Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation sustains momentum in multiple myeloma research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Lucy McDonald
Photography by Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital Illumination Gala

Multiple myeloma treatments have significantly improved over the past two decades, thanks in part to the driving engine of transformational philanthropy. This is particularly true at Dana-Farber, where physician-scientists have developed new tools to address historically intractable cancers like multiple myeloma, a rare cancer of the bone marrow. Through revolutionary basic, translational, and clinical research, Dana-Farber researchers have transformed a multiple myeloma diagnosis—now patients often live three to five times longer than they might have expected only two decades ago. Despite this tremendous progress, there is still much work to be done, as multiple myeloma cells grow resistant over time to even the most potent medicines.

New treatments are developed through an arduous process beginning at the laboratory bench and ending years later with drug delivery at a patient’s bedside. What propels therapies through this pipeline is philanthropy. Paula and Rodger Riney of St. Louis, who in 2019, through their Foundation, made the single largest award supporting multiple myeloma research in Dana-Farber history, understand the distinctive power that philanthropy holds. The Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation has been a dedicated supporter of Dana-Farber and with their latest grant of more than $1.5 million has cumulatively contributed more than $60 million to the Institute.

“We are in awe of what Dana-Farber has achieved in multiple myeloma care over the past two decades.”

Rodger Riney

“We are in awe of what Dana-Farber has achieved in multiple myeloma care over the past two decades,” said Rodger Riney. “The future holds so much promise. We are proud to continue supporting research that will bring forth new treatment options for multiple myeloma patients.”

The Riney Foundation’s most recent grant funds a project led by Carl Novina, MD, PhD, investigating a transcription factor called NFκB that binds to DNA to turn on the genes that produce antibodies. Abnormal NFκB regulation is a common attribute of several cancers including multiple myeloma. Novina’s team is identifying natural RNAs that bind to NFκB and is studying their effect on NFκB function. Moreover, these RNAs will be used to build novel RNA-based therapies that mediate NFκB destruction that could be developed into more durable therapies to combat drug resistance.

 “New therapies are essential to continue making progress against cancers,” said Novina. “Committed supporters like The Riney Foundation are key to expanding our research to identify new options that can make a difference in patients’ lives.”

title.rendered: Campbells advance research into rare ovarian cancer

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kathy Clute

Emily Campbell was just 32 when she began seeing doctors in her hometown of Miami for vague symptoms—abdominal discomfort and bloating, low appetite, fatigue—that were dismissed by her local medical team until she insisted on an ultrasound scan. That led to a diagnosis of low-grade serous ovarian cancer and surgery to remove her reproductive organs.

Facing the prospect of post-surgical chemotherapy, Emily was alarmed that her physicians had little familiarity with her cancer. “For the number of times I was in the hospital and the doctor would say, ‘I’ve never seen this before’ or ‘This is rare,’ I was thinking, we have to find a doctor who sees this every day,” said Emily.

Their search led them to Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the Division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber. After a new pathology workup at the Institute, Emily learned that she instead had borderline ovarian cancer, for which surgery is currently the only treatment option.

“It completely changed the trajectory of my life,” Emily said. “When you are given a diagnosis like low-grade serous carcinoma, your body and your mind kind of go into shock.” Learning that she would not have to go through chemotherapy was a huge relief.

But during the time they were seeking second opinions and researching ovarian cancer, Emily and her husband, Chris, realized that there’s a real dearth of information about borderline and low-grade forms of the disease, which are typically found in younger women.

“It’s really not studied enough and there are just not enough resources,” said Emily. “I wanted to know if it was going to come back in five years, or never. I wanted to know how this cancer grows or changes.”

That’s a big reason why the couple made a $1.5 million gift in 2023 to establish the Campbell Family Fund for Borderline and Low-Grade Ovarian Cancer Research at Dana-Farber. This will fund Matulonis’ work to understand the spectrum of the diseases, identify at-risk patients earlier, expand treatment options, and improve the quality of life for patients.

Chris explained that they chose Dana-Farber particularly because Matulonis had a project ready to go. “The team had clear goals for this research, and they were clear about what they needed in order to make the project come to life,” he said. “We met with the team last summer, and to see the amount of work they’d already done and see their excitement was really energizing. The biggest thing for us was knowing that it was going to move the needle.”

“We are so grateful for this vital support from Emily and Chris,” said Matulonis. “Their gift is incredibly impactful, given that only a fraction of ovarian cancer research funding is directed to the borderline or low-grade serous subtypes.”

title.rendered: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants spur cutting-edge MDS research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Scott Edwards
Photography by Sam Ogden

In 2019, Dana-Farber established the Edward P. Evans Center for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) with generous funding from the Edward P. Evans Foundation. The foundation recently awarded new grants totaling $1.35 million to three Dana-Farber scientists for novel investigations into MDS, a group of blood disorders caused by abnormal bone marrow stem cells.

Benjamin Ebert, MD, PhD, co-director of the Evans Center, chair of Medical Oncology, and the George P. Canellos, MD, and Jean S. Canellos Professor of Medicine, received a Discovery Research Grant to address critical challenges in MDS research. To develop new therapies for MDS, better preclinical models are needed to guide the design of clinical trials. Ebert will use two different genome editing approaches—CRISPR-Cas9 and CRISPR-Cas12—to build more advanced mouse models of MDS to study the numerous genetic mutations driving the disease.

“We hope that multiplexed editing of genes will provide better models of MDS and that this will ultimately lead to robust preclinical studies to guide effective clinical trials,” says Ebert.

Christopher Reilly, MD, and Mounica Vallurupalli, MD, each received Evans MDS Young Investigator Awards, which are geared toward early career scientists looking to establish their own labs as MDS investigators.

Reilly, director of the Multidisciplinary Telomere Biology Disorder Program, is examining the process by which individuals with short telomeres—the protective ends of chromosomes that prevent DNA damage—develop MDS. His project will determine which types of mutations occur in people with short telomeres and how these mutations lead to MDS.

With her grant, Vallurupalli is studying mutations in the splicing factor gene SF3B1, which impair red blood cell production, a hallmark of MDS. She will develop models that systematically test which genetic factors help to overcome impaired red blood cell production in SF3B1-mutated bone marrow stem cells.

“Dana-Farber has been, and continues to be, one of our most valuable partners.”

Michael Lewis, Edward P. Evans Foundation

“The Edward P. Evans Foundation considers our support of the highly innovative work in Benjamin Ebert’s laboratory, and our support of early investigators, such as Christopher Reilly and Mounica Vallurupalli, as one of the best investments we can make to discover new knowledge that will enable the development of effective MDS treatments,” says Michael Lewis, president of the Edward P. Evans Foundation. “Dana-Farber has been, and continues to be, one of our most valuable partners to achieve this goal, and we are excited to see what these efforts might yield.”

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, was recognized as the Edward P. Evans Investigator in MDS research at Dana-Farber at an event in 2023.

img.alt_text: Coleman Lindsley and Michael D. Lewis pose for a photo with a framed lab coat at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants propel MDS research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation, which funds the most promising research in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), a type of blood cancer, has awarded grants totaling $2.325 million to five Dana-Farber researchers who are pursuing innovative MDS strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kesslers expedite research to expand treatment options for AML
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A crucial infusion of funds from Michele and Howard Kessler is enabling the clinical trial of a promising combination treatment.

title.rendered: GivingTuesday inspires thousands to defy cancer

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

For many, Thanksgiving weekend marks the start of the holiday season, with family gatherings and a spirit of gratitude in the air. Since 2012, GivingTuesday celebrates this special time of year by encouraging charitable giving on the Tuesday after Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping. Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund participated again in 2023, with over 4,800 supporters across the country donating more than $1.7 million to The Dana-Farber Campaign to fund lifesaving research and care and further the Institute’s mission to defy cancer.

To inspire further giving, Arbella Insurance Group matched the first $50,000 in donations contributed that day.

GivingTuesday provides flexible funding that Dana-Farber deploys across the Institute to the most promising projects and most critical needs. Contributions help improve outcomes for patients like Tilly, who was featured during the campaign. Tilly was just 2 years old when she was diagnosed with an inoperable low-grade glioma in her spinal cord. Her parents were devastated, but upon bringing her to Dana-Farber, the family found little pieces of joy and gratitude during her time at the Jimmy Fund Clinic.

Throughout her treatment, Tilly enjoyed the opportunities to play and just “be a kid” at the Jimmy Fund Clinic, dressing in costumes, a different character for each of her weekly visits. Some days she would be Brucey the Monkey or Doctor Tilly. Some visits she would come dressed as a cow, or a unicorn, or even Elton John, and always with a box of doughnuts to share with the nurses and staff at the Jimmy Fund Clinic.

Tilly just turned 5 years old and is doing great. Her chemotherapy treatments slowed the tumor’s growth, and while she will continue to be monitored every 12 weeks for the foreseeable future, as of now her prognosis is good.

“Dana-Farber has become not just a place where Tilly gets treatment, llama cookies, and stickers, but also the place where she becomes the living proof.”

Josh Danoff

“Dana-Farber has become not just a place where Tilly gets treatment, llama cookies, and stickers, but also the place where she becomes the living proof,” said her father, Josh Danoff. “We have experienced the loss of so much, but we still have our daughter, she is still with us. And no matter how hard the day is, no matter what her physical challenges in her life may be, we will have another day, another opportunity for things to get better.”

All funds raised on this special day of giving help ensure that adults and children with cancer can go on to live, rich, fulfilling lives during and after treatment—even as a doctor, a monkey, or a glam rocker, like Tilly.

jetpack-related-posts.title: GivingTuesday raises $1.7 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year on the Tuesday following Thanksgiving, Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund participates in a worldwide celebration of generosity known as GivingTuesday. And each year, thousands of generous supporters step forward in response.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Your generosity on GivingTuesday is fueling the next victory over cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2012, GivingTuesday was created with one simple goal: encourage generosity and collective giving. What was once a small experiment in communal impact is now a worldwide movement comprised of donors who support causes close to their hearts.

img.alt_text: Pediatric patient wearing a pink tutu

jetpack-related-posts.title: Your generosity soars past $2 million on GivingTuesday
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On GivingTuesday 2024, Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund’s community of support far surpassed our $1 million goal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation recently made a generous $200,000 gift to support a variety of research and patient care programs at Dana-Farber. The funds will drive innovative prostate and pancreatic cancer research while enhancing social services offered to pediatric patients and grieving families.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo in front of mountains

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sally Naser Charitable Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Sally Naser Charitable Foundation, led by Camille and Robert Naser, made a $200,000 gift in support of early career investigators whose research drives breakthroughs, improves patient outcomes, and advances pediatric sarcoma care and research. This gift builds upon many years of support in honor of their daughter, Sally.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

title.rendered: Expect Miracles Foundation continues to drive discovery

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Robbie Merritt
Photography by Evelyn Dow Photography

For the 29th year, Expect Miracles Foundation reaffirmed their support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute with a gift of $1 million. This latest gift brought the foundation’s cumulative total to more than $14 million toward our shared mission of defying cancer.

The Expect Miracles Discovery Fund—one of three philanthropic branches of the foundation—specifically supports the Robert and Renée Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science at Dana-Farber, which collaborates with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners to bring basic scientific breakthroughs to market in the form of new cancer drugs and therapies, a key strategic priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign. The Belfer Center is unique in that it joins scientific discovery with academic and industry research to solve the most common and challenging drug development problems and accelerate the availability of cutting-edge cancer treatments.

“Because of the philanthropic support from Expect Miracles Foundation, the Belfer Center is able to take its work to the next level,” says Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Belfer Center and the David M. Livingston, MD, Chair at Dana-Farber. “Cancer is an incredibly complex set of diseases, but with continued funding, we are able to better understand and unravel these complexities and bring hope to patients around the world with challenging cancers and few effective treatment options.” Jänne is also the senior vice president for Translational Medicine and director of the Chen-Huang Center for EGFR Mutant Lung Cancers at Dana-Farber.

“Our donors should be proud, knowing they are part of a community that is improving the lives of cancer patients everywhere and making miracles happen every day.”

Frank Strauss, Expect Miracles Foundation

Each year, Expect Miracles Foundation brings together professionals in the financial services industry to participate in a variety of exciting events that not only raise critical funds for lifesaving cancer research but also advance the financial and emotional health of those impacted by cancer. Two large signature golf tournaments are highlights each year: the East Coast Classic, which teed off for the 29th year in June at Pinehills Golf Course in Plymouth, Mass.; and the Atlantic Coast Classic, which marked its sixth year at Fiddler’s Elbow Country Club in Bedminster, N.J.

“We at Expect Miracles Foundation are beyond proud to support the lifesaving work happening at Dana-Farber,” says Frank Strauss, founder and chairman of Expect Miracles Foundation. “Our donors should be proud, too, knowing they are part of a community that is improving the lives of cancer patients everywhere and making miracles happen every day.”
