title.rendered: Prevention is goal of groundbreaking immunotherapy trial

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sasha Pedro

When asked what motivates her to support cancer research, Susan Hertog starts at the beginning, when her best friend was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer at the age of 49.

It was 1994, and research was still years away from the robust understanding we have today of the genetic drivers of cancer. Immunotherapy treatments were not yet available. Genetic testing was in its infancy. Years later, in the mid-2000s, Susan herself was diagnosed with early stage breast cancer and lived firsthand the marked improvements in treatments. She would call herself lucky, but asserts that it’s more than luck—it’s the brilliance of researchers and clinicians constantly working to improve cancer care.

These experiences inspired Susan and her husband, Roger, to begin supporting cancer research, through philanthropic gifts to research initiatives around the country, and through Susan’s position on the board of directors of the Breast Cancer Research Foundation.

The Hertogs know the critical role that prevention plays in cancer care, and the critical role that Dana-Farber is playing in this space—prevention is a key strategic priority for the Institute and The Dana-Farber Campaign. In support of these efforts, the Hertogs gave $1 million to fund the prevention-focused INteRCEPT trial led by Glenn Hanna, MD. This is one of the first-ever studies evaluating the efficacy of immunotherapy in cancer prevention for patients with high-risk oral precancerous disease.

In 2021, Hanna and his colleagues identified a population of oral precancerous patients who may benefit from immunotherapy. Now, a phase 2 clinical trial is underway to test a new injectable immunotherapy agent as a method of preventing progression to oral cancer.

“We previously have shown that patients with a high-risk precursor condition that progresses to oral cancer in up to 80% of patients, have precancerous tissues rich with immunologic cells and inflammatory T cells,” said Hanna, who serves as director of the Center for Cancer Therapeutic Innovation and the Center for Salivary and Rare Head and Neck Cancers at Dana-Farber. “Thanks in part to Susan and Roger’s generous funding, we are now testing targeting these cells with new immunotherapy drugs.”

While the INteRCEPT trial is primarily focused on oral cancer, the results have the potential to be adapted to other precancerous conditions, such as those that lead to gastrointestinal, pancreatic, and skin cancers.

“We were intrigued because the object of Dr. Hanna’s study is prevention and early intervention, which is critical to the study of any form of cancer,” said Susan. “Metastasis, at this moment in time, is incurable. Dana-Farber’s emphasis on catching cancer early is important, and impressive.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such…

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Building on past support, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 physician-scientists at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

title.rendered: Hyundai Hope On Wheels invests in innovative treatments for children

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Caroline de Lacvivier
Photography by Debbie Gravina Photography

Since 1998, Hyundai Motor America and Hyundai Hope On Wheels have represented a powerful engine of support for pediatric cancer research. As part of its mission, Hyundai has a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, both as a presenting sponsor of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk for more than two decades, and as a major grant funder, contributing nearly $17 million to propel the Institute’s pediatric cancer research. In 2023, HHOW made two grants totaling $650,000 to Rani George, MD, PhD, and Nina Weichert-Leahey, MD.

With her funds, George is studying a potential therapeutic vulnerability for metastatic osteosarcoma, a hard-to-treat bone cancer most common in adolescents and young adults, characterized by impaired DNA repair mechanisms. Her hypothesis is that metastatic osteosarcoma cells depend on CDC5L, a protein that prevents the accumulation of deleterious levels of DNA damage, thereby allowing these cancer cells to proliferate. George suspects that this dependency could be targeted with compounds known as degraders, which could bring a new treatment to a patient population that has not seen an improved survival rate in 40 years.

“We are grateful to the dedicated researchers, doctors, and medical institutions receiving grants as we work together to move closer to a cure.”

John Guastaferro, Hyundai Hope On Wheels

Weichert-Leahey is leveraging her grant to explore combination therapies to boost the effects of retinoic acid in neuroblastoma, a pediatric tumor of the network of nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. While retinoic acid is an effective maintenance therapy for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma, resistance develops, leading to disease relapse. Weichert-Leahey believes that KAT6 inhibition may enhance the effects of retinoic acid, and given that KAT6 inhibitors are already in clinical development for adult tumors, has significant potential for translation in pediatrics.

“Over the past 25 years, Hyundai Hope On Wheels has been creating hope for families facing childhood cancer by investing in life-saving research, treatment, and support,” said John Guastaferro, executive director, Hyundai Hope On Wheels. “To date, we have contributed $225 million in our mission to end childhood cancer. We are grateful to the dedicated researchers, doctors, and medical institutions receiving grants as we work together to move closer to a cure.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back on course with the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

img.alt_text: Walkers and volunteers on the route of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk steps into record-breaking year with over $11.2 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On a sunny Sunday in October 2025, the Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s signature fundraising event, crossed more than just the finish line at Boston Common.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnston gift paves the way for a novel ovarian cancer clinical trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Debbie Johnston is dedicated to supporting causes that are close to her heart, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ovarian cancer research is one such cause.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk celebrates 35 years of inspiration and impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last fall, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patients, families, and supporters joined forces to defy cancer at the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, which raises the most money of any single-day walk in the nation.

img.alt_text: A group of Jimmy Fund Walk participants pose for a photo in their Walk t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk defies cancer with $9.4 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to more than 8,400 participants, the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk surpassed $185 million in funds raised over 37 years for Dana-Farber's lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo, with one person holding a framed t-shirt with signatures

title.rendered: OOFOS steps up for breast cancer research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

In fiscal year 2023, active recovery footwear brand OOFOS donated $626,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Project Pink initiative, a special program that supports breast cancer research by donating a percentage of online sales to the Institute.

Project Pink was inspired by Duncan Finigan, the former brand leader and marketing director of OOFOS. Finigan was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer in 2014, and the initiative launched a year later in 2015. Though Finigan passed away in 2019, OOFOS continues Project Pink to honor her legacy and continue spurring progress in breast cancer treatments at Dana-Farber.

“We are so grateful to OOFOS and their customers for their partnership over the years, which is making a real difference in the lives of patients and their families,” said Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, chief of the Division of Breast Oncology in the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers at Dana-Farber, and an important partner of Project Pink. “Thanks to this support, we have been able to advance new treatments and deepen our understanding of the mechanisms that drive breast cancer and metastasis.”

“Duncan continues to inspire us every day, and we are just getting started.”

Lou Panaccione, OOFOS

In addition to money raised from online sales, OOFOS also donates pairs of recovery shoes to the Institute, as well as every year giving a pair to each runner on the Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge team—all in honor of Finigan, an avid runner. And in 2023, OOFOS sponsored two cows in the CowParade New England presented by Herb Chambers, a summer-long event to help celebrate the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary.

“When we started Project Pink, we wanted to do anything we could to help Duncan, so in many ways, the cause chose us,” said Lou Panaccione, CEO and co-founder of OOFOS. “What has grown from that show of support for Duncan is a remarkable, year-round partnership with Dana-Farber through which we have donated more than $3.6 million. Duncan continues to inspire us every day, and we are just getting started.”

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Jane Anderson

Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

Rally’s grants span many forms of cancer. In T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, Birgit Knoechel, MD, PhD, is investigating how leukemic cells interact with the immune system, how chemotherapy affects the immune system’s capacity to fight cancer, and how the immune system affects outcomes. Kimberly Stegmaier, MD, is expanding her preclinical studies to evaluate the effectiveness of potential new targeted drugs in pediatric leukemia.

In neuroblastoma, Nina Weichert-Leahey, MD, studies how the efficacy of retinoic acid, a current treatment for the disease, can be enhanced by the addition of PF-9363—an inhibitor of the KAT6 enzyme—and how this combination treatment stops cancer growth. In germ cell tumors, which span children, adolescents, and young adults, Lindsay Frazier, MD, and collaborators are working to genomically profile tumors across a range of patient backgrounds to better understand the different causes of the disease and how to best tailor treatments.

Riaz Gillani, MD, is studying the germline genetics and tumor genomics of Ewing sarcoma with the goal of better understanding risk and improving treatment for this aggressive cancer in pediatric and adolescent patients. In a form of kidney cancer called tRCC, Srinivas Viswanathan, MD, PhD, aims to learn how TFE3 fusions drive cancer and find drugs to counteract them.

As philanthropic seed investors in the next great discovery, the Rally Medical Advisory Board continues to be impressed with the innovative grant proposals submitted by Dana-Faber researchers. Each grant is chosen by a rigorous dual peer-review process. Rally hopes these projects will bring us closer to better treatments with fewer long-term side effects and, ultimately, a cure.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sajni Fund raises vital funds for rare pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds raised help to advance personalized immunotherapy for DIPG, a rare and aggressive pediatric brain tumor.

title.rendered: DeFeo gift aims to push ovarian cancer treatment to next level

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Alain Martinez

The late Dara Frigoletto DeFeo was a giver, her husband, Peter DeFeo, recalls fondly. Whether it was reading to small children in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic or helping a senior citizen pluck an item off a high shelf at the grocery store, Dara “had a unique way to communicate that she cared.”

So, when ovarian cancer claimed her life in June 2023 at age 57, Peter was determined to carry on her legacy of giving. He established the Dara L. Frigoletto DeFeo Fund for Ovarian Cancer Research with a $500,000 gift to Dana-Farber last August, initiating a philanthropic plan he and Dara had mapped out during the last two years of her life.

“One person can make a difference,” said Peter, a Natick resident who co-founded VetCor, which acquires and operates veterinary practices in the U.S. and Canada. “And if you empower a lot of people, a lot of people can make a difference. We really thought we could do that, so when Dara passed, I committed myself to getting things off the ground very quickly.”

“It’s sad that cancer is the second leading killer in our country every year,” he said. “The reassuring thing is knowing that there’s real hope and real treatment. But you need dollars to keep that momentum going, to push research to that next level.”

Physician-scientist Elizabeth Lee, MD, who was Dara’s oncologist, agreed. “Dara was truly a vibrant, selfless person,” she said. “Her namesake research fund will be instrumental in helping us detect ovarian cancer, understand the biology of its subtypes, and treat it. We are so grateful.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

jetpack-related-posts.title: GivingTuesday raises $1.7 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year on the Tuesday following Thanksgiving, Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund participates in a worldwide celebration of generosity known as GivingTuesday. And each year, thousands of generous supporters step forward in response.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods supports families facing cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donations from HomeGoods and Homesense shoppers at more than 900 locations nationwide funded cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber team defies cancer in ASICS Falmouth Road Race
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Aug. 21, more than 330 members of Dana-Farber’s team ran seven miles along the scenic Cape Cod coastline for the 50th running of the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

title.rendered: Patricia Farah’s legacy continues through support for cancer research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Shannon Watterson
Photography by Sam Ogden

Patricia Farah’s driving motivation was always to make an impact. This was clear to her husband, Alfred, who predeceased her, and to her long-time financial advisor, Jay Lupica, who recently made a $500,000 gift from Patricia’s estate in support of the Patricia W. and Alfred E. Farah Borderline and Low-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer Research Fund and the Patricia W. and Alfred E. Farrah International Term Fellowship, both at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Prior to her death in 2011, Patricia was charitably inclined, and wanted her dollars to continue to make an impact after she passed—both in Naples, Florida, where she and Alfred lived for the later part of their lives, and in their home of New England.

“Patricia knew research was a big piece of the puzzle to improving people’s lives,” said Lupica. When he heard about the research going on in Dana-Farber’s Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers, led by Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the Division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber, he knew these were the kinds of projects Patricia would be interested in: in-depth investigations at a world-class institution, where her money would make a big impact and have outsized benefits for patients, if successful.  

“Patricia knew research was a big piece of the puzzle to improving people’s lives.”

Jay Lupica

Patricia’s legacy also makes an impact through the Patricia W. and Alfred E. Farrah International Term Fellowship, led by Alan D’Andrea, MD, director of the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers and of the Center for DNA Damage and Repair, who is training the next generation of researchers who are already making a material difference in patients’ lives.

“Patricia was very interested in helping women and children,” Lupica explains. “I feel it is my responsibility to carry on her goals, and these projects that Ursula and Alan are leading are exactly what she should have enjoyed supporting, were she alive.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chubb gift advances ctDNA research for cancer detection and therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $750,000 gift, Patricia and Steve Chubb established The Alice Fund to support Parsons’ research into ctDNA and her lab’s efforts to develop technologies to overcome current limitations.

jetpack-related-posts.title: DeFeo gift aims to push ovarian cancer treatment to next level
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The late Dara Frigoletto DeFeo was a giver, her husband, Peter DeFeo, recalls fondly. Whether it was reading to small children in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic or helping a senior citizen pluck an item off a high shelf at the grocery store, Dara “had a unique way to communicate that…

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of Dara Frigoletto DeFeo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnston gift paves the way for a novel ovarian cancer clinical trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Debbie Johnston is dedicated to supporting causes that are close to her heart, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ovarian cancer research is one such cause.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift to ovarian cancer inspired by story of research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In early 2022, Dr. Jean Kasmer read a story in Impact about an ovarian cancer survivor who gave to support the research of Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

title.rendered: Dana-Farber recruits largest B.A.A. Half Marathon® team to date

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

The 2023 B.A.A. Half Marathon® was a race to remember, with 650 participants running Sunday, Nov. 12, to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s race toward a cancer-free future. Members of Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund’s team came from 29 states and 5 countries to conquer this crisp, 13.1-mile fall run through Boston’s Franklin Park and Emerald Necklace Park System. Each participant beamed with pride, knowing that they had a hand in raising more than $767,000 to advance research and care for cancer patients everywhere.

Many team members run and fundraise with Dana-Farber’s team because they themselves have been affected by cancer or are looking to honor a loved one who has been impacted by this terrible disease. Some fundraise as individuals, while others, like Team Nick Strong, fundraise as a group within Dana-Farber’s charity team. Team Nick Strong was created in 2022 to honor Nick Gaspar, a 15-year-old patient in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic who was fighting brain cancer. Sadly, Nick passed away in May 2023, but his mother, Jennifer Gaspar, returned this season with her sister-in-law, Jessica Gaspar, and 41 other runners who raised over $59,000 in Nick’s memory.

“This was my first half marathon and first race ever,” said Jessica. “Witnessing the impressive turnout and seeing the funds raised in Nick’s honor fills me with great joy. Nick would undoubtedly take pride in our achievements.” The Gaspar family, along with all of Dana-Farber’s 2023 B.A.A. Half Marathon runners, are eager to continue to raise funds that will help find cures for all cancers. “Running has helped me through some of the hardest days,” said Nick’s mother, Jennifer. “Whenever I want to give up, I think of Nick and how he never quit. I hope to continue to raise awareness and funds for pediatric cancer so that someday kids can just be kids, without cancer.”

“I hope to continue to raise awareness and funds for pediatric cancer so that someday kids can just be kids, without cancer.”

Jennifer Gaspar

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s B.A.A. Half team runs 13.1 miles to defy cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The B.A.A. Half Marathon® returned to Boston’s Emerald Necklace on Sunday, Nov. 13, 2022, in person for the first time since 2019. Dana-Farber’s 2022 B.A.A. Half team included 485 team members running 13.1 miles, both in-person and virtually, to support Dana-Farber’s commitment to groundbreaking research and quality patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s Boston half team sets new record
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sunday, November 9, marked the Boston Athletic Association’s (B.A.A.’s) annual Boston Half, a scenic 13.1-mile race through Franklin Park and the Emerald Necklace Park System.

jetpack-related-posts.title: B.A.A. 5K®
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The B.A.A 5K® took place April 15, welcoming the largest team to date of Dana-Farber runners who collectively raised $184,271. Runners had the option to race in person on the 3.1-mile course that began and ended in the Boston Common, or run in their own neighborhoods as virtual teammates. The…

img.alt_text: B.A.A. 5K runners participating on Dana-Farber's team pose for a photo on the Boston Common

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber team defies cancer in ASICS Falmouth Road Race
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Aug. 21, more than 330 members of Dana-Farber’s team ran seven miles along the scenic Cape Cod coastline for the 50th running of the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

img.alt_text: Falmouth Road Race Team Power runners

jetpack-related-posts.title: Runners across the country race for Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2022 Run Any Race season roster consisted of 71 runners, running various races across the globe in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Andrew Kaczysnki of Team Beans on the course

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge raises nearly $7 million in support of Claudia Adams Barr Program investigators
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge (DFMC) attracts runners from across the globe as they take on 26.2 miles in support of innovative basic research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute each year.

title.rendered: Husband honors late wife with gift to support older breast cancer patients

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

In the last essay she would write for her college reunion book, Virginia Aisner quoted one of her favorite lines from Vergil’s Aeneid: “Perhaps, at some time, we shall be glad to remember even these things.”

To those who knew her, Virginia was not only an extraordinary mentor and friend, but also a person who steadfastly overcame life’s setbacks while bringing out the best in those around her. When she was diagnosed with early stage breast cancer in 2020, the news came as a shock to her and her husband, Jim, but she tackled this obstacle the way she did most things—with grace and resolve.

Sadly, despite an initially good prognosis, Virginia’s cancer returned a year later, and this time it was metastatic. She passed away in 2022 at the age of 77.

Breast cancer is a challenging diagnosis at any age, but for adults over age 70, a diagnosis brings unique challenges not faced by younger patients. And while Jim was grateful to the care team at the hospital where Virginia was treated, he believed there were a number of areas that needed improvement, from coordinating appointments and limiting waiting times, to opening channels of communication with oncologists and nurse practitioners.

Soon after Virginia had passed, Jim read a story in Impact about a new program launching at Dana-Farber, the Program for Older Adults with Breast Cancer, and saw that it addressed the problems Virginia had had during her treatment. As a result, he was inspired to establish a fund in her honor, to which he has now given $350,000 in support of this special program.

“This gift is a wonderful way for Virginia to be remembered,” said Jim. “But beyond that, for years to come and in a variety of ways, it will help other people in their journey with this complicated and difficult disease.”

“We take a multidisciplinary approach designed specifically for older patients, which includes support for other age-related health issues they may be facing, nutritional support, social workers, and much more,” said Rachel Freedman, MD, MPH, founder and director of the program. “We are grateful to Jim for honoring Virginia’s legacy in such a meaningful way. He is helping us fill a critical need for so many patients and their families.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Patricia Farah’s legacy continues through support for cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Patricia Farah’s driving motivation was always to make an impact. This was clear to her husband, Alfred, who predeceased her, and to her long-time financial advisor, Jay Lupica, who recently made a $500,000 gift from Patricia’s estate in support of the Patricia W. and Alfred E. Farah Borderline and Low-Grade…

img.alt_text: Two scientists having a conversation inside a lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: DeFeo gift aims to push ovarian cancer treatment to next level
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The late Dara Frigoletto DeFeo was a giver, her husband, Peter DeFeo, recalls fondly. Whether it was reading to small children in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic or helping a senior citizen pluck an item off a high shelf at the grocery store, Dara “had a unique way to communicate that…

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of Dara Frigoletto DeFeo

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS steps up for breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In fiscal year 2023, active recovery footwear brand OOFOS donated $626,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Project Pink initiative, a special program that supports breast cancer research by donating a percentage of online sales to the Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bowen’s legacy gift provides unrestricted support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bowen's generous bequest shows the impact one individual can have on cancer research and care for people around the world.

title.rendered: Fallon gift helps advance epigenetic research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Dave Derosches

Real estate executive Mike Fallon wasn’t a cyclist or a Dana-Farber donor when David Fialkow invited him to a fundraising dinner for the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) in the spring of 2022. By the time the event was over, however, he had made a financial commitment to the Institute and had decided to take part in the next PMC with his father, Joseph, founder of The Fallon Company.

“This all happened over the course of a few hours,” he said, explaining how moved he’d been when Dana-Farber’s Cigall Kadoch, PhD, shared news of her research into a misguided gene regulator that makes some childhood cancers resistant to treatment. “I was so excited by the promise of her work and her enthusiasm. I thought, I may not understand all of this, but if I have any kind of instinct about people who are onto something—she was onto something.”

Fallon, who is CEO of The Fallon Company, directed a portion of his gift to Kadoch’s research, which advances one of The Dana-Farber Campaign’s key priorities: epigenetics, the study of changes in how genetic material is read and processed by the cell, rather than changes in the DNA itself. Dana-Farber researchers are at the forefront of revolutionary research into how to block or reverse these changes, while playing a lead role in FDA approval of the first-ever epigenetic drug to treat solid tumors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating PMC Heavy Hitters
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the run-up to the 2024 Pan-Mass Challenge on Aug. 3-4, the PMC celebrated top fundraisers from the 2023 ride, known as "Heavy Hitters,” who raise 65% of the PMC’s annual gift.

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the Pan-Mass Challenge's record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024.

img.alt_text: Bicycle riders on an unpaved path in the woods

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Cyclists participating in the PMC Winter Cycle at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back in the saddle again, 2022 PMC raises record $69 million—that’s $900 million since 1980!
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The world can always use more good news, so here is something great—the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the annual bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the country, had its best year yet, raising a record $69 million for Dana-Farber in 2022.

title.rendered: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Cyrena Musset
Photography by Rebecca Dufault

Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000. This CGA will support the Mellen and Eisenson Family Fund for BRCA Research and Clinical Trial Support and help our expert faculty continue to provide exceptional research and clinical care to patients with BRCA-mutated and BRCA-related cancers, well into the future.

The concept is simple: you make a donation using cash or appreciated securities and, in turn, Dana-Farber pays you a fixed amount for life. At the end of your lifetime, the remainder of your gift becomes part of your legacy and supports our efforts to defy cancer through The Dana-Farber Campaign and beyond.

Eisenson encourages all those interested in giving to Dana-Farber, and in particular other Trustees, to establish their own CGA. “A CGA is not in place of a current gift, but rather it’s a better and simpler way for the Institute, and for us, to make a meaningful gift we would otherwise make in our wills,” said Eisenson. “CGA rates are also the highest they have been in over a decade, making this the perfect time to make such a gift.”

title.rendered: Planned gift in honor of late husband will help patients access care

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Alison Krawczyk

As a nurse in Boston, Theresa Kennedy knew of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s impeccable reputation for patient care. However, when her late husband, Ken Packard, was diagnosed with multiple myeloma and treated at Dana-Farber, the compassion and kindness they received far exceeded their expectations. “Almost to a fault, everyone we encountered was so kind and on top of everything,” said Kennedy. “We always felt like they were taking care of their own family member.”

During his treatment with Jacob Laubach, MD, MPP, chief of the Division of Multiple Myeloma, and Ginger Dalton, MS, APRN, Packard came to enjoy his visits and talking with them about his passion—pizza—and the book he was writing on the subject. In memory of Packard, Kennedy gives annually to support Laubach’s multiple myeloma research.

Additionally, Kennedy included a gift of $200,000 to Dana-Farber in her estate plans through her individual retirement account (IRA) to support the Patient Assistance Fund, which helps patients who don’t have the ability to pay for their health care or associated costs. “I don’t have an estate that can build a building, but we had an incredible social worker who helped us navigate the cancer experience,” said Kennedy. “It’s tragic when people can’t get good care because they can’t access it. I hope this gift will help.”

“We always felt like they were taking care of their own family member.”

Theresa Kennedy

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift honors late wife and supports multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kenneth Nirenstein remembers his late wife, Harriet, as wise, elegant, and graceful. After Harriet’s passing, seeking a way to keep her memory alive while also making a difference to others, Kenneth made a gift of $100,000 to establish the Harriet Shapiro Nirenstein Fund for Multiple Myeloma Research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of an ocean

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber 2024 Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Event attendees explored Dana-Farber's patient-first approach to cancer care with Institute leaders and special guest Doris Kearns Goodwin.

img.alt_text: Glenn Hanna, MD (left), and Doris Kearns Goodwin

jetpack-related-posts.title: International Myeloma Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received a $250,000 Translational Research Award from the International Myeloma Society and the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation. This support will advance his innovative work to combat disease relapse in multiple myeloma patients following CAR T-cell therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hazel B. Harrington Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. title.rendered: The Herb Chambers Companies surpasses $1 million in gifts

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by Debbie Gravina Photography

The Herb Chambers Companies, one of New England’s largest auto dealers, has been a powerful ally and supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund since 2015. In 2023, the company surpassed $1 million in cumulative giving after serving as presenting sponsor for the Jimmy Fund’s keystone 75th anniversary event, CowParade New England.

Herb Chambers has sponsored numerous Jimmy Fund events and programs over the years, including Jimmy Fund Golf, Dana-Farber UnMask Cancer, Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl,® and the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, in addition to offering the official Red Sox Foundation/Jimmy Fund License Plate in their Massachusetts dealerships and hosting Boston Marathon® parties for customers, with proceeds benefitting research and care for Dana-Farber patients and families.

The company’s unrestricted gifts are especially valuable because they provide flexible funds that are deployed to support the Institute’s most promising projects and most pressing needs. “We are extremely proud to have contributed over $1 million in support of cancer care and research at Dana-Farber since 2015,” said company President Herb Chambers. “This is a cause that means so much to our employees and customers alike. We feel fortunate to be doing our part to contribute in the fight against cancer.”

“This is a cause that means so much to our employees and customers alike. We feel fortunate to be doing our part to contribute in the fight against cancer.”

Herb Chambers, The Herb Chambers Companies

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies continued their support of Dana-Farber as Premier Sponsor of the Jimmy Fund in 2024. Their continued partnership has been felt across marquee Jimmy Fund events since 2015, resulting in over $1 million of cumulative support for Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Herb Chambers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over three sunny days in June, more than 10,000 enthusiasts gathered to enjoy unlimited ice cream, with proceeds supporting Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Two longstanding supporters receive the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans at a special Fenway Park ceremony.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CowParade New England MOOves the needle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The cows of CowParade New England presented by Herb Chambers are MOOving to new pastures after a successful, summer-long event celebrating the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary with the Greater Boston community.

img.alt_text: People pose with colorful umbrellas and a dog in front of a painted cow sculpture

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS steps up for breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In fiscal year 2023, active recovery footwear brand OOFOS donated $626,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Project Pink initiative, a special program that supports breast cancer research by donating a percentage of online sales to the Institute.

title.rendered: Expanding equitable access to critical care

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Stephanie Lowitt

Last year, the National Breast Cancer Foundation (NBCF) generously provided $155,000 to support Dana-Farber’s inclusion, diversity, and equity work to ensure equitable health outcomes for all. The foundation’s partnership is helping to reduce barriers to care, to promote breast health education, and to ensure historically underserved patients have timely access to medical and logistical support.

The funding fully supports a breast cancer patient navigator position, a role that serves as a lifeline for patients, ensuring that they understand their diagnosis and what treatment options are available, and safeguards integrated care throughout their treatment. The navigator acts as a liaison to help make certain that highly prevalent socioeconomic barriers do not act as a deterrent to patients’ completion of treatment or the quality of care that they receive.

NBCF’s generosity is further helping remove barriers to care through patient assistance funds, enabling critical interventions to address the basic needs of breast cancer patients including food and transportation support. This gift also supports Dana-Farber’s Mammography Van, the only mobile digital mammography van in Massachusetts, which brings state-of-the-art breast cancer screenings and breast health education directly to medically underserved individuals throughout Greater Boston. Since 2002, the van has provided more than 43,000 mammograms.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Taco Bell Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Taco Bell Foundation awarded $135,000 in 2024 to support Taco Bell Scholars in Dana-Farber’s Workforce Development Student Training Program, which is dedicated to building a more diverse, inclusive, and equitable workforce; increasing access and reducing barriers to careers in health care; and training the next generation of health care…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation gave $200,000 in support of the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP) at Dana-Farber. With these funds, the CCEP team will continue to address disparities in health care for underserved patient populations and pursue equitable care for every cancer patient.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Khannas’ generous gift helps breast cancer patients navigate care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Homai Khanna and her family are improving access to Dana-Farber's high-quality care with generous support for the Patient Navigator Program.

img.alt_text: A person wearing a mask and pointing to words on a sign

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: AstraZeneca awarded over $360,000 to Dana-Farber to appoint a patient navigator to expand equitable access to clinical trials within the Breast Oncology Research Program. This navigator will proactively engage with patients with breast cancer and will focus on outreach and education to patients from historically marginalized communities to help navigate…

title.rendered: Gift honors late wife and supports multiple myeloma research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Sami Eisenberg

Kenneth Nirenstein remembers his late wife, Harriet, as wise, elegant, and graceful. After Harriet’s passing, seeking a way to keep her memory alive while also making a difference to others, Kenneth made a gift of $100,000 to establish the Harriet Shapiro Nirenstein Fund for Multiple Myeloma Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of Paul Richardson, MD, director of clinical research at the Jerome Lipper Multiple Myeloma Center and the R.J. Corman Professor of Medicine.

Harriet was one of Richardson’s patients who benefitted from clinical trials, and Kenneth aims to give hope to other patients who are diagnosed with multiple myeloma through this gift.

“Harriet and I were always very humbled when we were at Dana-Farber to see all the different patients being treated for various types of cancer,” he said. “Many of these patients would come in from all over the world to receive this extraordinary care, and we were lucky enough to have it in our own backyard.”

Kenneth is grateful for the exceptional care his wife received and is optimistic that the gift made in her honor will have a lasting impact. “The research taking place at Dana-Farber is changing lives every day, and I hope this gift can help play a role in finding a cure for this terrible disease.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Changing the trajectory of multiple myeloma and access to care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Joan Suzanne Tomsich was just 48 years old, she thought her life was over. A diagnosis of multiple myeloma led her to thoughts like, “Will I be around to see my kids graduate or witness them getting married?”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Planned gift in honor of late husband will help patients access care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As a nurse in Boston, Theresa Kennedy knew of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s impeccable reputation for patient care. However, when her late husband, Ken Packard, was diagnosed with multiple myeloma and treated at Dana-Farber, the compassion and kindness they received far exceeded their expectations.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people sitting and wearing Pan-Mass Challenge t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: Smith Family support inspires others to help speed multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Paul Richardson has found an important partner in Robert and Dana Smith, who recently made a $3 million gift to continue supporting his advanced MM clinical trials research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: R.J. Corman Railroad Group, LLC
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: R.J. Corman Railroad Group, LLC contributed $100,000 to the work of Paul Richardson, MD, to accelerate new multiple myeloma therapies for patients. This generous gift builds on the longstanding partnership with R.J. Corman and the Corman family, which stretches back more than 20 years and began with the company’s founder,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: International Myeloma Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received a $250,000 Translational Research Award from the International Myeloma Society and the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation. This support will advance his innovative work to combat disease relapse in multiple myeloma patients following CAR T-cell therapy.

title.rendered: Lindsley named Edward P. Evans Investigator

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, was recognized as the Edward P. Evans Investigator in MDS research at Dana-Farber at an event in 2023. Lindsley’s lab focuses on the biology and treatment of myeloid malignancies, with specific emphases on defining genetic pathways of progression, mechanisms of familial leukemia predisposition, and understanding donor and recipient factors that drive clinical outcomes after bone marrow transplantation. The event also celebrated the Edward P. Evans Foundation, which established both the investigatorship and the Edward P. Evans Center for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) at the Institute with a visionary $5 million grant, the largest gift to MDS research in Dana-Farber history.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation, which funds the most promising research in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), a type of blood cancer, has awarded grants totaling $2.325 million to five Dana-Farber researchers who are pursuing innovative MDS strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign dramatically advanced the prevention, early detection, and interception of cancers on a wide variety of fronts.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2019, Dana-Farber established the Edward P. Evans Center for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) with generous funding from the Edward P. Evans Foundation. The foundation recently awarded new grants totaling $1.35 million to three Dana-Farber scientists for novel investigations into MDS, a group of blood disorders caused by abnormal bone marrow…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cure Childhood Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, received a $220,000 Early Investigator Award from CURE Childhood Cancer. This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. The grant also helps launch her career as an…

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. In September, participants rode routes of 30 or 50 miles starting and ending at Camp Mah-Kee-Nac in Lenox, Mass. This vital “spoke in the wheel” of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) presented by the Red Sox Foundation and M&T Bank contributed more than $944,000 to the PMC’s record-breaking gift of $72 million in 2023 and its cumulative total of $972 million raised since 1980. The PMC is the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser and the Institute’s largest single contributor, accounting for 62% of the Jimmy Fund’s annual revenue.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the Pan-Mass Challenge's record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024.

img.alt_text: Bicycle riders on an unpaved path in the woods

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge is moving to Worcester
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which has raised $1.125 billion for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute since 1980, is relocating its starting line and hub site from Sturbridge to Worcester.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Michael Blanchard

“Sparking Discoveries Through the Power of Community” was the theme for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium in October 2023—a powerful reminder in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary year of the impact made by our generous community across the country and around the world over many decades. Supporters and leaders gathered for updates on key priorities of The Dana-Farber Campaign including how AI can benefit patients, how the Institute is accelerating drug development, and how Dana-Farber is advancing patient-centered care, especially for medically vulnerable communities.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program…

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Liposarcoma Research Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defy cancer celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Defy Cancer Celebration at Fenway Park on Sunday, March 30, was a day filled with hope, progress, and community. It highlighted the impact and innovation in cancer care and research made possible by gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign from 2017 to 2024.

img.alt_text: People at Fenway Park during the Defy Cancer celebration event

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Data science and AI allow us to better match patients to clinical trials, identify disparities in cancer care, and pinpoint the most promising treatment options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Brittany Flaherty
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

When The Dana-Farber Campaign was announced in 2021, cancer early detection and interception represented a key priority to re-imagine cancer care and it remains so today. In December 2023, Dana-Farber launched the Centers for Early Detection and Interception, a first-of-its-kind, integrated clinic that brings together clinicians and researchers across cancer types to advance early detection of precancerous conditions and to prevent cancer from arising in individuals at increased risk.

Today, cancer is often diagnosed when a patient has symptoms and the disease is already advanced, which can result in higher mortality. When patients have access to screening and we can detect disease earlier, we have a greater chance of treating that cancer. Prostate cancer, for example, was the most common new cancer diagnosis in 2023 and remains the second most deadly cancer in men. However, when this disease is diagnosed early, the five-year survival rate is close to 100%.

Dana-Farber has deep expertise in early detection and prevention. Examples include pioneering discoveries on hereditary cancer risk and developing one of the first clinical cancer genetics and prevention programs in the world. Building on this momentum and with advances in genomics and data science, philanthropy is enabling new approaches and expanded access to proactive care—saving more lives and improving the quality of life for people everywhere and for generations to come.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Join Us
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic effort that will forever change cancer research and care.

title.rendered: Enduring impact through endowed chairs at Dana-Farber

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Brittany Flaherty

One of the most powerful ways that donors can make a lasting difference is by endowing a faculty position in perpetuity through establishing a Dana-Farber Chair. A key priority for The Dana-Farber Campaign, endowed chairs honor and recognize distinguished faculty members, provide invaluable financial support, and act as an important tool to retain and recruit world-class talent.

During The Dana-Farber Campaign, generous donors have established 18 new Dana-Farber Chairs—more than doubling the number of Dana-Farber endowed chairs since the start of the campaign in 2017. The newly established chairs provide support for leaders in cancer prevention, cancer care equity, nursing, psychosocial oncology and palliative care, head and neck oncology, leukemia, lymphoma, colorectal cancer, and more.

“Holding this chair is one of the greatest honors of my professional career. Even more so, that it was made possible by the Lunder Family, whom I have known and whose friendship I have treasured since childhood, has truly touched my heart.”

Richard Stone, MD, Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber

Dana-Farber is home to a vast community of passionate experts across an enormous range of disciplines whose lifesaving research requires sustained support. Among the most important investments in the acceleration of scientific discovery is the talent brought to bear at the laboratory bench and the patient bedside—our “human capital.” An endowed donor-named chair enables our distinguished faculty members to explore truly novel ideas and conduct research that will lead to transformative discoveries in cancer science and improved outcomes for our patients.

To learn how to establish an endowed chair and more about the impact of endowed support, visit DefyCancer.org/exceptional-expertise/.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Baila Janock embodies generosity in its many forms. For over 30 years, she has combined her gifts of time, treasure, and talent to make a long-lasting impact on Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and its patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Brittany Flaherty
Photography by Amy Baugess

Patients around the world are counting on Dana-Farber to make cutting-edge discoveries and address the greatest mysteries in cancer research. Why do some cancers become resistant to treatment? Why do certain drugs work for some patients but not others? How can we detect more cancers at an earlier, treatable stage?

Epigenetics research is helping us answer these crucial questions. In fact, epigenetics is a key priority for The Dana-Farber Campaign and many scientists believe it is the next frontier in cancer medicine. But what is epigenetics?

For decades, cancer research has focused on genes and how changes to the genetic sequence—changes to our DNA—can drive cancer. However, we now know that DNA is only part of the picture.

Epigenetics literally means “above the genes.” Epigenetics research focuses on changes in gene expression or cell function that are not due to changes in the DNA sequence itself, but in how cells read the DNA sequence. Often caused by environmental or external factors like stress, infection, or toxin exposure, epigenetic changes can impact which genes are “expressed”—meaning which genes are turned on or off—including genes involved in cancer.

Consider this: a butterfly has the exact same DNA sequence as the caterpillar it developed from. Its metamorphosis is due to epigenetic changes in which genes are expressed. The same genetic information can result in very different outcomes—caterpillar or butterfly—depending on which genes are turned on or off.

In the same way, each human cell contains the exact same DNA. And like a butterfly, our genes can be expressed in different ways. Normal expression leads to normal cell function, but epigenetic changes or errors can cause cells to “forget” their normal function, which can lead to cancer.

However, we know these changes can be reversed. Epigenetic therapies can help a cell “remember” its identity and restore its function. They can also stop cancer cells from resisting treatment or even enable physicians to detect cancer at an earlier stage.

Dana-Farber is a pioneer in this field. Our scientists have made breakthroughs that led to some of the world’s first epigenetic therapies, including treatments that stop drug resistance in a type of sarcoma and block epigenetic changes in a form of pediatric leukemia.

With generous support through The Dana-Farber Campaign, we can build on this momentum and leverage our unique expertise to pursue research at the forefront of discovery, ultimately allowing us to transform care for patients everywhere.

excerpt.rendered: Patients around the world are counting on Dana-Farber to make cutting-edge discoveries and address the greatest mysteries in cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate gift accelerates cancer care and research for years to come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Out of gratitude for the excellent care received by his late wife, Gerry Martineau left a generous bequest to support research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: $10 million gift brings rare cancers to the fore
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Linde Family Foundation has made a transformative $10 million gift to Dana-Farber to launch the Center for Therapeutic Discovery, which will develop novel therapies for patients with rare and hard-to-treat cancers.

img.alt_text: Graphic depiction of MLL complex proteins

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palumbo family moves needle for patients with rare pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On the cusp of Chad Palumbo’s senior year of high school in 2022, he found himself in an unexpected place: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Chad had been diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma, a rare form of soft tissue cancer that appears mainly in children and teens.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Radical collaborations target intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: BTC has awarded $22.9 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers working across multiple institutions to unlock the secrets of four difficult-to-treat cancers and intercept or develop cutting-edge treatments for them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Impact Staff

Congratulations to Lori Dougherty, our long-time Impact editor, on her retirement in January. Over the course of 13 years with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Lori oversaw the creation of 55 issues of Impact, 12 issues of Honor Roll, and 11 issues of Milestones—bringing her signature excellence and thoughtfulness to every issue. The care with which she shared these stories demonstrates her dedication to Dana-Farber’s mission, to our patients, and to our unparalleled community of support. Thank you, Lori, for shaping Impact into a meaningful and beautiful magazine that recognizes the generosity of others and serves as an inspiration to our donor community near and far. We wish you all the best in your next chapter!

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When I first stepped into my role at Dana-Farber in 2019, I was immediately struck by the endless compassion and dedication of the people around me.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Anna Fuller Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Anna Fuller Fund has made a wonderful impact with a $150,000 gift to support breast cancer research conducted by Evanna Mills, PhD, at Dana-Farber. The investment will fuel investigations to better understand risk factors for triple-negative breast cancer with the potential to inform the development of more effective treatments.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Brittany Flaherty

The Dana-Farber Campaign is our ambitious, multibillion-dollar fundraising effort to change the future of cancer research and care—the largest in the Institute’s history and one of the largest ever in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. Our community of support is crucial to this effort.

Harnessing the Power of Data and AI
Data science and artificial intelligence (AI) are key priorities for The Dana-Farber Campaign because advances in these technologies allow us to better match patients to clinical trials, identify disparities in cancer care, and pinpoint the most promising treatment options. For example, Eli Van Allen, MD, chief of population sciences, and his colleagues developed a deep learning model that accurately predicted which prostate cancer patients would develop treatment resistance. Even more exciting, the model identified an existing drug that could help overcome this resistance, leading to the launch of a new Dana-Farber-led clinical trial.

We aim to raise $55 million through the campaign to harness the full power of data science and AI to unlock countless advancements across cancer genomics, immunotherapy, early detection, cancer care equity, and more. Together, we can develop innovative technologies that change lives around the world.

To learn more about the power of data, visit DefyCancer.org.

excerpt.rendered: Data science and AI allow us to better match patients to clinical trials, identify disparities in cancer care, and pinpoint the most promising treatment options.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024

Dear Friends,

When I first stepped into my role at Dana-Farber in 2019, I was immediately struck by the endless compassion and dedication of the people around me. Year after year, event after event, breakthrough after breakthrough, the Dana-Farber and Jimmy Fund community shows up in great numbers and with great generosity. This community is truly changing the future of cancer care.

We know that Dana-Farber is special, and The Dana-Farber Campaign has given us an opportunity to expand our reach and grow our community—making an important difference to patients who need us. As one example, I was so inspired to see that more than 8,400 people participated in the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai—sharing their time and support to advance our mission. It was a moving reminder that people are the key to our success. People drive progress.

On that note, I want to take a moment to congratulate one of our own on 13 years of service to this incredible community. Our longtime Impact editor, Lori Dougherty, retired in early January. For more than a decade, Lori helped bring stories of donor generosity to life on the pages of Impact. Her work behind the scenes played an important role in supporting our lifesaving mission, and all of us are wishing her the very best in her next chapter.

Thank you, all of you, for your role in bringing the next breakthroughs to our patients. I look forward to seeing what we accomplish next—together.

Sincerely,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer
