jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past seven years, The Dana-Farber Campaign has enabled incredible progress at the Institute, the effects of which ripple out to help patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to the tenacity and generosity of our entire community over the last seven years of The Dana-Farber Campaign, we are defying cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Dr. Sidney Farber achieved the first remissions in childhood leukemia in 1947, he changed everything.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: We are thrilled to unveil the Spring 2023 issue of Impact—the first of our newly redesigned magazine and website!

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

The American Gastroenterological Association awarded $300,000 to support a Dana-Farber study into pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), an aggressive disease that currently has limited and short-lasting treatment options. This funding will enable Jeffrey Patterson-Fortin, MD, PhD, to gain insights into how PDAC responds to immune-based therapies that could provide longer term benefit for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation's generous grant of $100,000 supports the research of Dana-Farber’s Harshabad (Harsh) Singh, MBBS. This funding empowers him to further explore the biological foundations of HER2-driven gastric tumors and test innovative therapies. This can potentially transform treatment approaches for this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their latest commitment of $300,000, the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is supporting the work of Dana-Farber’s Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD, who aims to identify the mechanisms of response or resistance to a combination treatment for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CLL Global Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. This funding will help advance their studies of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aiming to uncover new insights and improve treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

Spring 2024
By Shannon Watterson

With a $250,000 gift, Julie Wallace Bennett established the Peter Warren Fund for Pancreatic Research, in honor of her partner, Peter. Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber will lead this research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leon and Leslie Asadoorian
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Leon and Leslie Asadoorian gave $100,000 to advance gastrointestinal cancer research under the direction of Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. Their support will help expand Wolpin’s team of clinical trial experts, enabling them to increase patient enrollment and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation gift focuses on cancer interception
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $1.25 million gift to Dana-Farber from the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation supports research focused on ways pancreatic cancer might be detected—and intercepted—before it can be seen on CT scans or other imaging modalities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kendall Family prioritizes innovation in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In cancer research, hope can be realized in how we innovate. Inventive clinical trials can lead to novel approaches and new, accessible medicines that ultimately bring better outcomes to patients.

Spring 2024
By Robin Orwant

The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation recently made a gift of $125,000 to support metastatic breast cancer (MBC) research under the direction of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. This gift enables Abravanel and his team to leverage cutting-edge profiling technologies, such as single-cell sequencing and spatial profiling, to develop personalized and effective treatments…

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation gave $125,000 in support of research led by Paolo Tarantino, MD, which seeks to improve the precision of antibody-drug conjugates. This funding will aid Tarantino in unlocking new insights into metastatic breast cancer, with the intention of identifying additional treatments for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded grants totaling $412,400 to support studies into genetic and epigenetic changes that occur in cancer progression, with the goal of identifying new therapeutic targets.

Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Carol and Peter Clark made a $300,000 estate gift through their donor-advised fund and charitable remainder trust to support the Jimmy Fund. The Clark Family has long supported the Jimmy Fund through the Jimmy Fund WMass Classic golf tournament and other fundraising and volunteer activities.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Robin Orwant

The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation recently made a generous $200,000 gift to support a variety of research and patient care programs at Dana-Farber. The funds will drive innovative prostate and pancreatic cancer research while enhancing social services offered to pediatric patients and grieving families.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sally Naser Charitable Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Sally Naser Charitable Foundation, led by Camille and Robert Naser, made a $200,000 gift in support of early career investigators whose research drives breakthroughs, improves patient outcomes, and advances pediatric sarcoma care and research. This gift builds upon many years of support in honor of their daughter, Sally.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation gift focuses on cancer interception
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $1.25 million gift to Dana-Farber from the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation supports research focused on ways pancreatic cancer might be detected—and intercepted—before it can be seen on CT scans or other imaging modalities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Novel clinical trial in pancreatic cancer bolstered by $1 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Byrnes is a self-proclaimed “satisfied customer.” Diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer in 2015, John is grateful for each and every day his Dana-Farber care team has given him.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Casey Repasy

Dunkin’ Joy in Childhood Foundation made a grant of $200,000 to launch the Dogs for Joy program at Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund. This initiative provides in-residence dogs to pediatric patients, helping with tasks like motivating children to get out of bed for a walk or even demonstrating how to put on a hospital gown.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk defies cancer with $9.4 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to more than 8,400 participants, the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk surpassed $185 million in funds raised over 37 years for Dana-Farber's lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo, with one person holding a framed t-shirt with signatures

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: FDA approves new pediatric brain cancer drug
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Support for The Dana-Farber Campaign advanced research leading to approval of the new treatment for pediatric low-grade glioma (PLGA).

img.alt_text: A doctor smiles and listens to the heartbeat of a young patient

jetpack-related-posts.title: One Mission
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2023, One Mission contributed $189,000 to Dana-Farber, reinforcing its long-standing dedication to pediatric cancer patients. This contribution enhances the wellbeing of young patients through the Pediatric Resource Program as well as family-centered initiatives like the Jimmy Fund Clinic Festival, a Parent Bereavement cruise, and other special events for patients…

Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Alex Studios

Eva and Erick Eigner have pledged to give and raise a total of $300,000 to further research led by Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, in the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center exploring the microbiome and the use of machine learning and artificial intelligence to identify risk factors, and to support the center’s patient and family forum.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rasmussen Family funds research into underlying causes of colorectal cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Anna and Neil Rasmussen are no strangers to medical research in the quest to find answers to chronic illness—one of their children had been living with ulcerative colitis since she was seven years old.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Neil and Anna Rasmussen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Neil and Anna Rasmussen’s $250,000 gift supports the groundbreaking colorectal cancer research of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, at Dana-Farber. Their generous support over time has already exceeded $1 million. This most recent gift focuses on the microbiome’s role in the disease’s development and treatment in patients under 45, aiding personalized…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Russ Agrusa honors late wife by fueling colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Russ and his late wife, Paula, established the Project P Fund in 2014 with a goal of empowering researchers at Dana-Farber to develop more effective targeted and immune-based therapies for patients with colorectal cancer. Since Paula’s death in 2016, Russ has continued to honor her legacy through ongoing support for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Dan Jaffe support Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and her husband, Dan Jaffe, renewed their support for the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber to help stem the disease’s dramatic rise among people under 50.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society targets improved treatments and access
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded $1.12 million in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers seeking to answer those questions and more.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Kayla Carcone
Photography by Sam Ogden

Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded $224,000 to support investigations led by Sylvan Baca, MD, PhD, and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, into circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). This research will analyze tumor features and aims to, for the first time, guide therapy selection in breast cancer with low levels of ctDNA.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $224,000 grant, Innovation in Cancer Informatics is funding a project at Dana-Farber that will develop and pilot a new mobile health application that integrates patients’ electronic health records to better support them, and their care teams, in management of advanced cancer pain.

title.rendered: The Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Shannon Watterson

The Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research gave a generous grant to support research by Jose Orozco, MD, PhD, into the role of sugar-sensing pathways in metabolic adaptation. These studies may reveal a new therapeutic target to alleviate metabolic maladaptive responses to the chronic overconsumption of sugars and carbohydrates.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Crowley gift accelerates innovative research in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley are longtime supporters of Dana-Farber who made their first gift nearly two decades ago to advance melanoma research in memory of Brian’s sister.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Liposarcoma Research Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brian and Jane Crowley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

Spring 2024
By Casey Repasy
Photography by 13 Photography

Keep Smiling Beautiful is a 5K race hosted by the family of Chelsea Smith, to champion research into hepatocellular carcinoma—liver cancer—by Chelsea’s doctor, Allison O’Neill, MD, at Dana-Farber. Each year, in Chelsea’s honor, O’Neill runs this 5K which has raised more than $115,000 since 2017.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Young patient inspires new fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In a video recorded in early 2021, a then 12-year-old Orli Wildman Halpern explained to a live New York Times audience over Instagram the experience of living with, and through, treatments for hepatoblastoma, a rare liver cancer primarily seen in toddlers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Children’s Cancer Research Fund made two grants totaling $350,000 to support an early phase trial for relapsed pediatric liver cancer led by Allison O’Neill, MD, and liquid biopsy research in rhabdomyosarcoma led by Brian Crompton, MD. These pivotal resources help to develop more effective precision therapies for children facing…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jog for Julie
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: girlygirl P.A.R.T.S. surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The girlygirl P.A.R.T.S. 5K/Walk for Ovarian Cancer has surpassed $1 million in total funds raised since 2009, supporting research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PHASE ONE Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PHASE ONE Foundation awarded $370,000 to support a Dana-Farber clinical trial led by Alison O’Neill, MD. The clinical trial aims to test a new intratumoral delivery method for a novel immunotherapy in pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory solid tumors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hope Scarves
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD, received $115,000 from Hope Scarves in 2023 to support his investigations on the evolution of metastatic breast tumors and the mechanisms they use to evade treatment. This work promises to help transform the treatment of the disease in years to come.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brenda McAdam
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare…

img.alt_text: A closeup photo of a couple

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yoseph Linde
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Yoseph Linde renewed his support of Dana-Farber with a recent gift of $100,000 to advance bile duct cancer research under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. This latest gift, in honor of his late wife Haya, supports Cleary’s team’s continued in-depth DNA and RNA sequencing work to better understand…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Bayer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Bayer gave $100,000 to establish The Bayer Family Research Fund. The fund aims to accelerate discoveries into safer, more effective and durable treatments for patients facing Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a rare form of blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Michael Blanchard

A new $1 million gift from Rev. Dr. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy will advance the work of Irene Ghobrial, MD, a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and the Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers to better understand risk factors for multiple myeloma and develop interventions to stop the disease from progressing.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2020, Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine endowed three Dana-Farber Chairs in support of prevention and early detection research at the Institute, with a gift to The Dana-Farber Campaign.

img.alt_text: Catherine Wu, MD; Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; and Jonathan Lavine

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign dramatically advanced the prevention, early detection, and interception of cancers on a wide variety of fronts.

img.alt_text: Researchers at work in the Centers for Early Detection and Interception.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Paving the way to cancer prevention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Wycliffe “Wyc” Grousbeck and Emilia Fazzalari are firm believers that “good things don’t come easy.” As philanthropic and entrepreneurial leaders in the Boston community, they seek out innovative and exceptional people who are tackling groundbreaking endeavors that are simply too compelling to refuse.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oliver S. and Jennie R. Donaldson Charitable Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Donaldson Charitable Trust gave nearly $195,000 to support the PROMISE study led by Irene Ghobrial, MD. This nationwide study aims to better understand the higher rates of a multiple myeloma precursor condition in older adults who are Black or who have a close family member with blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CLL Global Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. This funding will help advance their studies of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aiming to uncover new insights and improve treatment…

Spring 2024
By Casey Repasy

Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised $281,332 in 2023 for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber. Every year, Little League baseball and softball players in New England raise vital funds for the Jimmy Fund during this summer league, making a significant impact in the fight against cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised more than $272,000 for Dana-Farber in its 39th season. New England’s young baseball and softball players extended their Little League® seasons to take a swing at cancer by raising vital funds for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2022 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to John Berardi (second from right), program director of Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports, which rallies thousands of youth baseball and softball players each summer to fundraise for the Jimmy Fund in their communities…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by the Yawkey Foundation surpassed its $275,000 goal, contributing $359,476 of unrestricted funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and underscoring the Yawkey Foundation’s dedication to advancing care for its community. The top fundraising team was North Reading 10U Gold, raising $18,465, and the top individual fundraiser, James Keohan, raised $10,617.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Shannon Watterson

After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yoseph Linde
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Yoseph Linde renewed his support of Dana-Farber with a recent gift of $100,000 to advance bile duct cancer research under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. This latest gift, in honor of his late wife Haya, supports Cleary’s team’s continued in-depth DNA and RNA sequencing work to better understand…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people outside on a balcony

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mulligan Family Fundraiser
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mulligan Family organized a birthday fundraiser for Dana-Farber in honor of their loved one, Patrick. They raised over $15,000 to help James Cleary, MD, PhD, standardize screening options and uncover more effective treatments for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cox Family continues support of Dana-Farber’s revolutionary science
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Career venture capitalist and Institute Trustee Howard Cox and his wife, Wendy Cox, are no strangers to the revolutionary science and clinical treatments happening at the Institute.

Spring 2024
By Robin Orwant

Five Dana-Farber investigators were recently awarded more than $250,000 from the National Cancer Center (NCC), whose mission is to provide financial support to researchers undertaking innovative and promising studies that seek to cure cancer. Since its founding 70 years ago, NCC has granted nearly $8 million in cancer research funding.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CRI grants accelerate immunotherapy research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) is advancing bold new strategies to harness the immune system against cancer through two grants at DanaFarber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating advanced and aggressive kidney cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Kidney Cancer Association (KCA) has made $650,000 in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers who are unlocking the molecular mechanisms of a disease that will be diagnosed in nearly 82,000 U.S. residents this year and claim the lives of more than 14,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rosenberg Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Rosenberg family has made a generous gift to support patients through all aspects of the breast cancer journey. Their gift funds triple-negative breast cancer research led by Elizabeth Mittendorf, MD, PhD, MHCM; research training led by Harold Burstein, MD, PhD; infusion nursing directed by Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Impact You Have Made Possible
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute aspires to provide the care and treatment our patients deserve. We are able to achieve these ambitions because of our dedicated donor community.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lung Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $150,000 grant from the Lung Cancer Research Foundation supports William Feng, PhD, in investigating AP-1 transcription factors as a potential “Achilles’ heel” in KRAS-mutant lung cancer. His research aims to develop a novel AP-1–targeted therapy to overcome drug resistance and improve outcomes for patients with this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: LUNGevity Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With grants totaling $400,000 from LUNGevity Foundation, Jaclyn LoPiccolo, MD, PhD, is researching prediction of genetic lung cancer risk in people under 45 and how risk factors may guide screening and therapeutic approaches; and Elliot Brea, MD, PhD, is exploring how a modified CAR T-cell therapy may be effective in…

Spring 2024
By Kayla Carcone

Dana-Farber recently received a $100,000 grant from Oligo Nation to advance vital research on oligodendroglioma, a rare type of brain tumor. This grant propels efforts to develop treatment strategies to target dependencies conferred by IDH oncogenes in this disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Casey Repasy
Photography by Josh Campbell

In 2023, One Mission contributed $189,000 to Dana-Farber, reinforcing its long-standing dedication to pediatric cancer patients. This contribution enhances the wellbeing of young patients through the Pediatric Resource Program as well as family-centered initiatives like the Jimmy Fund Clinic Festival, a Parent Bereavement cruise, and other special events for patients at the Jimmy Fund Clinic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A caravan of good cheer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Red Sox brought some welcome warmth and inspiration to the pediatric cancer patients at the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Red Sox mascot Tessie with a pediatric patient

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: FDA approves new pediatric brain cancer drug
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Support for The Dana-Farber Campaign advanced research leading to approval of the new treatment for pediatric low-grade glioma (PLGA).

img.alt_text: A doctor smiles and listens to the heartbeat of a young patient

jetpack-related-posts.title: Together in action, together in progress: Giving Day surpasses fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year’s annual Giving Day marked an especially generous occasion for dedicated supporters of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Creating community for adolescent and young adult patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each day, nearly 50 adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients—those between the ages of 15 and 39—come to Dana-Farber for treatment, but many never connect with one another because they wait for appointments on different floors.

By Colleen Sullivan

With their latest commitment of $300,000, the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is supporting the work of Dana-Farber’s Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD, who aims to identify the mechanisms of response or resistance to a combination treatment for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network recently awarded $400,000 in grant funding to Institute researchers Julien Dilly, MS, and William Freed-Pastor, MD, PhD, to better understand mechanisms of response and resistance to KRAS inhibition in pancreatic cancer and improve existing pre-clinical models for this intractable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick made a generous gift to support pancreatic cancer research by Srivatsan Raghavan, MD, PhD, before Kevin’s passing from pancreatic cancer in July 2023. This generous contribution reflects their desire to help Dana-Farber uncover new treatment options and improve outcomes for all patients facing pancreatic cancer.

img.alt_text: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick sitting on a rock in front of the ocean

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dale Fishman
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dale Fishman gave $243,000 to fuel pioneering research led by Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD; Catherine Wu, MD; and physician-scientists across Dana-Farber. Fishman’s multifaceted philanthropy is empowering these investigators to advance novel cellular therapies for pancreatic cancer and personalized cancer vaccines, while bolstering the Faculty Research Fund, which together pave the…

Spring 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography courtesy of the Thoracic Foundation

The Thoracic Foundation awarded grants totaling $160,000 to Dana-Farber in 2023, to honor the wishes of foundation trustee Bradley Cook, who passed away in 2022. Brad, alongside his peers at the Thoracic Foundation, has been a steady funder of thoracic cancer research and instrumental in the nearly $900,000 the foundation has given over the years to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ruth (pictured) and Shelly Bramson made a generous gift of more than $100,000 to support the work of Jacob Sands, MD, a physician in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. This gift is enabling Sands and his team to continue developing and improving personalized therapeutic approaches for patients with thoracic…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Georgette and John Heerwagen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Coughlin Crew
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Michael Coughlin Lung Cancer Research Fund, established in memory of Michael Coughlin, recently surpassed $100,000 in funds generated in support of thoracic oncology at Dana-Farber. The majority of these funds were raised through the family’s Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk team, Coughlin Crew, which first participated in the event…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon supports bold research by emerging talent
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded $1.22 million in grants to four early career investigators at Dana-Farber whose research has the potential to yield important breakthroughs in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dr. Gerald and Mrs. Mary McGillicuddy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dr. Gerald and Mrs. Mary McGillicuddy made a $100,000 gift to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, a researcher in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. With this gift, Rotow and her team will work to develop better, more effective targeted and immunotherapy options for patients with…

Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography courtesy of the Tsai family

Polly and Ming Tsai made a generous new commitment to advance research by David Barbie, MD, and the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology designed to increase the durability, precision, and effectiveness of lung cancer treatments, like the promising CAR T-cell therapy already in development with previous support from the Tsais.

content.rendered:
Spring 2024
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Cresonia Wong Photography

With a gift of $100,000, Aaron Yuan established a fund in honor of his mother, Chaochi Yuan, to support BOLSTER, an educational and support program for ovarian cancer patients and caregivers led by Chaochi’s oncologist, Alexi Wright, MD, MPH; and to expand the program to include translation into Mandarin Chinese.

content.rendered:
Winter 2023

Dear Friends,

One of the things that makes Dana-Farber such a special place is our emphasis on teamwork. Collaboration enables progress—Dr. Sidney Farber fervently believed this and built a world-leading cancer institute around this pioneering philosophy over 75 years ago. Researchers and clinicians working together are at the heart of our bench-to-bedside approach; our partnerships around the globe speed scientific discovery; and every year, thousands of people come together to raise the funds that are crucial to our mission.

Teamwork is behind the incredible success of events like the Pan-Mass Challenge, which brought together thousands of riders, volunteers, sponsors, and supporters to raise an astounding $72 million this year, 100% of which will fund our lifesaving research and care. Our philanthropic partners collaborate with researchers and clinicians to improve outcomes for patients and families everywhere. Every single donation, large and small, speeds our progress.

When I look at the things that have been accomplished thus far since the start of The Dana-Farber Campaign, I am humbled by the remarkable philanthropic support that will advance strategic priorities of the Institute, provide permanent funding for our world-class faculty and clinical partners, and support programs that have a direct impact on patients today and in the future. Teamwork drives success—your enthusiasm and generosity in The Dana-Farber Campaign have proven that, and we are deeply grateful for your partnership. I wish you and your families a healthy and happy new year, and look forward to seeing what we accomplish together in 2024.

With gratitude,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Brittany Flaherty

The Dana-Farber Campaign is our ambitious, multibillion-dollar fundraising effort to change the future of cancer research and care—the largest in the Institute’s history and one of the largest ever in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. Our community of support is crucial to this effort.

Your Impact — Defy Cancer Fund
The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund. Cancer science changes every day, as do the needs of our patients. Gifts without restriction to a particular program fund areas that will make the greatest difference, in real time.

Many services that Dana-Farber offers to patients are not covered by health plans, yet can dramatically improve the patient experience and save lives. Examples include programs in prevention and early detection, financial assistance, community health, exercise and nutrition, psychosocial wellbeing, and survivorship.

Likewise, not every research program has adequate funding from traditional sources. The only way to advance groundbreaking scientific pursuits—especially in rare and difficult-to-treat cancers—is to offset the cost of research with unrestricted support. These flexible funds ensure that nothing can hold up our science—accelerating the pace of discovery and innovative, high-impact studies that speed new treatments to patients everywhere.

To learn more, visit DefyCancer.org.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic effort that will forever change cancer research and care.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Trustees Monica Chandra and Michael Eisenson in the hospital's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has played a critical role in the development of more than half of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the past 5 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defy cancer celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Defy Cancer Celebration at Fenway Park on Sunday, March 30, was a day filled with hope, progress, and community. It highlighted the impact and innovation in cancer care and research made possible by gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign from 2017 to 2024.

img.alt_text: People at Fenway Park during the Defy Cancer celebration event

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One way our supporters accelerate campaign efforts is by including Dana-Farber in their estate plans.

Winter 2023
By Katherine Agate
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

A generous $100,000 gift from Jonathan and Hope Ashner was made to support the research of Elizabeth Buchbinder, MD. The gift will help to fuel Buchbinder’s groundbreaking investigations into melanoma and maximize progress against the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Eileen Greisch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Matthew Miller
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Matthew Miller gave $100,000 to advance groundbreaking investigations in melanoma led by Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Miller’s support will help Haq uncover the genomic intricacies of drug resistance and explore new ways to enhance personalized medicine for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Blitzer renews support with generous new commitment to melanoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donor and patient advocate Michael Blitzer recently renewed his support of melanoma research at Dana-Farber with a $650,000 commitment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Malcolm and Luli MacNaught
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent gift of $100,000, Malcolm and Luli MacNaught continued their steadfast support for Dana-Farber’s F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, a pioneer in groundbreaking treatments for melanoma. Among these is the recent trial of a new combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors that allowed patients with metastatic melanoma to survive…

Winter 2023
By Lucy McDonald
Photography by Sam Ogden

Doron Broman, a Miami-based real estate developer and stage IV pancreatic cancer patient, has given $150,000 to support research in pancreatic cancer under the direction of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH. Broman came to Dana-Farber in 2015 with only months to live, but under the treatment of Ng, has defied the odds and is celebrating seven years since his diagnosis.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. Their support will help expand Wolpin’s team of clinical trial experts, enabling them to increase patient enrollment and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Neil and Anna Rasmussen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Neil and Anna Rasmussen’s $250,000 gift supports the groundbreaking colorectal cancer research of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, at Dana-Farber. Their generous support over time has already exceeded $1 million. This most recent gift focuses on the microbiome’s role in the disease’s development and treatment in patients under 45, aiding personalized…

With this contribution, and in honor of Eyring, Meyerhardt aims to refine treatment options…

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Katherine Agate
Photography by Sam Ogden

Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein made a generous gift in support of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole M. and Philip L. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. The gift will support Jänne and his team’s continued research into targeted therapies in lung cancer, novel EGFR inhibitors, and mechanisms of drug resistance, ultimately helping more patients and their families.

Winter 2023
By Lucy McDonald
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

Matthew Miller gave $100,000 to advance groundbreaking investigations in melanoma led by Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Miller’s support will help Haq uncover the genomic intricacies of drug resistance and explore new ways to enhance personalized medicine for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber exam room

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rare eye cancer is focus of new fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jonathan and Shelley Isaacson have made a $1 million gift to establish Dana-Farber’s first fellowship dedicated to the study of the disease, The Isaacson Family Fellowship in Ocular Melanoma.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: What is basic science?
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The first step in creating cutting-edge cancer treatments for patients is basic research—scientific investigation that uncovers biology’s fundamental principles and helps us understand how the cells and molecules in our bodies work.

img.alt_text: Close-up photo of a researcher looking through a microscope

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Shannon Watterson

Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases.

excerpt.rendered: Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR targets breast and uterine cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research recently awarded more than $1 million in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Nutrition Consortium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Nutrition Consortium awarded $110,000 to Dana-Farber to develop and test personalized nutrition plans for patients with cancer, aiming to improve their quality of life. This study will build on the guidelines previously established by the Cancer Nutrition Consortium.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

Winter 2023
By Shannon Watterson

The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation recently made grants totaling $200,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to fund two studies. One explores circulating tumor DNA at critical timepoints in early stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and the second assesses how chemotherapy effects the tumor-immune microenvironment and estrogen receptor activity in young women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation awarded $125,000 to Genevra Kuziel, PhD, supporting her research on estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, the most common breast cancer subtype with a high recurrence rate. Kuziel’s work aims to develop innovative combination therapies, with the goal of transforming treatment options and improving outcomes…

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation gave $125,000 in support of research led by Paolo Tarantino, MD, which seeks to improve the precision of antibody-drug conjugates. This funding will aid Tarantino in unlocking new insights into metastatic breast cancer, with the intention of identifying additional treatments for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Building on past support, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 physician-scientists at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

title.rendered: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Michael Quinn
Photography courtesy of Pan-Mass Challenge

On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both. Iconic spots along the ride evoke progress and pride, like Cherry Street, where the community motivates riders with high energy; the touching tributes to PMC Pedal Partners displayed on the stretch of road leading to the Lakeville water stop; and the dunes on the Cape, which spark a feeling of accomplishment when they finally come into view. At the same time, the PMC’s momentous fundraising milestones, surpassed year after year, enable equally ambitious advances in cancer research and care at Dana-Farber.

On August 5–6, the PMC hit a higher gear yet again during its 44th ride, as 6,500 riders from 44 states, territories, and districts and 6 countries pedaled 16 routes ranging from 25 to 211 miles across Massachusetts, or reimagined their rides in locations of their choosing. They were aided by more than 3,000 volunteers and 200 corporate sponsors, whose investment ensured that 100% of every rider-raised dollar goes directly to Dana-Farber. Nearly 1,000 cancer patients and survivors rode and volunteered as Living Proof of the PMC’s impact. Including funds raised in the PMC Winter Cycle, PMC Unpaved, and PMC Kids Rides, the committed PMC community generated a record-breaking 2023 gift of $72 million, bringing the organization’s cumulative total to an astonishing $972 million raised since 1980—putting the unprecedented $1 billion fundraising milestone squarely in sight for 2024.

“There’s a lot riding on the everyday heroes in the PMC community, and with their continued unwavering commitment to our mission we will keep bringing cures closer by the mile.”

Billy Starr, Pan-Mass Challenge

As Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, accounting for more than 62% of the Jimmy Fund’s annual revenue, the PMC remains the powerhouse for progress at the Institute, as it has for more than four decades, and is accelerating the success of The Dana-Farber Campaign. Philanthropy from the PMC helped Dana-Farber’s basic scientists discover the role of a protein called PD-L1 in blocking an immune attack on tumor cells, launching a new class of drugs called “immune checkpoint inhibitors” that revolutionized cancer immunotherapy.

PMC support also bolsters Dana-Farber’s clinical trials program, one of the largest in the country with more than 1,100 trials offered. Fueled in part by PMC funding, Institute investigators played a substantial role in the development of over half of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the last five years, including accelerated approval for a novel treatment for metastatic HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in 2023. Speeding these new medicines from the lab to clinics everywhere improves the lives of patients worldwide.

Resources from the PMC have also helped Dana-Farber’s Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP) double in size over the past year, expanding research-based interventions that alleviate health disparities, increase access, and enhance outcomes in medically underserved populations. This includes community-focused patient navigation, through which trained staff provide need-based assistance with transportation, language services, medical expenses, health insurance, nutrition, and other potential barriers to optimal care.

Such progress propelled by the PMC since its inception has helped many more people live better and longer with cancer, with the number of survivors in the United States growing from less than 5 million in 1980 to more than 18 million and counting today. This tremendous improvement exemplifies the PMC’s multifaceted impact on Dana-Farber’s important work and everyone who benefits. Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Dana-Farber president and CEO, the Richard and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine, and 8-year PMC rider, said: “All of us at the Institute are truly inspired by and grateful for the PMC’s extraordinary support, which empowers every life-changing advance we achieve.”

The PMC is determined to do even more to help Dana-Farber go the distance against cancer. “There’s a lot riding on the everyday heroes in the PMC community,” said Billy Starr, founder and executive director of the PMC and a Dana-Farber Trustee. “And with their continued unwavering commitment to our mission we will keep bringing cures closer by the mile.”

excerpt.rendered: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Wheeling in the years: The Pan-Mass Challenge produces origin story video
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, to mark its 45th ride and to celebrate crossing a phenomenal $1 billion in lifetime fundraising, the PMC created a film bringing its origin story to life.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: A group of bicycle riders riding along a wooded path

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Feb. 4, hundreds of riders assembled at Fenway Park’s 521 Overlook venue for the PMC Winter Cycle.

img.alt_text: Cyclists on stationary bikes at the 2023 PMC Winter Cycle

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Bikers on stationary bikes at the PMC Winter Cycle event

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge is moving to Worcester
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which has raised $1.125 billion for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute since 1980, is relocating its starting line and hub site from Sturbridge to Worcester.

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.
